Chapter 33 SD/EMMC Controller (SDMMC)
This chapter's module description applies only to the CH32H417, CH32H416 microcontroller product.
The system provides one SDMMC controller host/slave interface with a maximum transmission clock of 200MHz.
It supports 1-wire, 4-wire, and 8-wire communication modes, as well as dual-edge sampling. External devices such
as SD/TF cards and eMMC cards can be connected. Application code can flexibly configure various parameters
including data transmission/reception commands, response packet formats, valid data packet modes and lengths,
and dual-buffer length switching thresholds.
Note: When using 1-wire or 4-wire mode, unused data lines corresponding to GPIO pins cannot be repurposed for
output. They may be used for input multiplexing or as general-purpose GPIO outputs.
33.1 Main Features
 Support SD physical layer 1.0 and 2.0 specifications, as well as UHS-I SDR50, DDR50, and SDR104 modes
compliant with SD 3.0 specifications
 Compliant with EMMC Card Specifications 4.4 and 4.5.1; supports HS200 and HS400 modes per EMMC
Card Specification 5.0
 Communication modes support single-wire, four-wire, and eight-wire configurations
 Maximum communication clock single-edge up to 200MHz, dual-edge up to 180MHz
 Support dual-edge sampling
 Flexible configurable packet length, command format, and response status
 Provide hardware-automated clock stop function during data block intervals
 Support SD cards, SDIO cards, eMMC cards, and other devices compliant with SD interface protocols
 Support SDIO slave interface, enabling data exchange with chips featuring SDIO host interfaces
 DMA dual-buffering capability
33.2 Register Description
33.2.1 Communication Clock
 Frequency configuration
The controller interface provides two clock modes: low-speed mode and high-speed mode. Generally, the SD
protocol stipulates that the communication clock of about 400kHz should be used for the early initialization of the
equipment with SD interface to ensure better communication compatibility. When the parameter information of the
external equipment is obtained, it can be switched to a higher clock frequency for communication according to its
internally supported configuration.
Set the bit9 of R16_EMMC_CLK_DIV register to select the clock mode, and set the bit[4:0] frequency division
value to get the final SDIO interface output clock. Bit8 controls whether the EMMC peripheral outputs a clock
signal to the MSDCK pin, and it is necessary to ensure that the IO mode of the MSDCK pin is configured as push-
pull output.
 Phase configuration
When communicating with external SDIO interface devices, due to high clock frequency, hardware wiring, device
characteristics and other factors, signal sampling errors will occur.
The system SDIO controller's host interface provides an output clock phase inversion (180° offset) function. Setting
V1.8 726

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
bit 10 of register R16_EMMC_CLK_DIV to 1 physically inverts the output clock signal, while the controller's
internal clock remains unchanged. This method allows adjustment of communication timing.
Note: At higher SDCLK frequency, if the recommended timing adjustment register value can't communicate stably,
users need to initiate a bus sampling tuning sequence to find a better sampling point.
33.2.2 Command Sending and Response
The 48-bit data packet with fixed command length sent by SDIO host interface to slave machine is transmitted
serially on MCMD line. Some commands don't need the slave to respond, and some commands need the slave to
respond to reply packets or data packets with different lengths.
 General command format: Start bit (0)+ Transmission bit (1)+ Command index+ Parameter +CRC7+ End bit
(1)
The start bit, data bits, CRC7, and stop bit are automatically filled by the hardware. The command index and
parameters vary depending on the command and must be passed to the hardware controller by the application code.
Configure the parameter field in the SD command by writing to the R32_EMMC_ARGUMENT register; Writing
bits [5:0] of the R16_EMMC_CMD_SET register populates the command index, while bits [11:8] of this register
configure the hardware's expected response packet detection for this command. Writing to the
R16_EMMC_CMD_SET register triggers the hardware to transmit the command packet sequence on the MCMD
signal line.
 Short Response Format: Start bit (0) + Transmission bit (0) + Command Index + Parameters + CRC7 + Stop
bit (1)
 Long Response Format: Start bit (0) + Transmission bit (0) + Reserved field (111111b) + Data + Stop bit (1)
Slave response packets are categorized by length into 48-bit and 136-bit packets, with 32 bits and 128 bits of user-
valid data respectively. After sending a host command, the R16_EMMC_INT_FG register can be queried. If the
RB_EMMC_IF_CMDDONE flag is set to 1, the R32_EMMC_RESPONSE register can be read to obtain the valid
data from the slave interface response packet. If the response packet is abnormal, corresponding flags in bits [2:0]
of the R16_EMMC_INT_FG register will be set.
33.2.3 Read Multiple Data Blocks Consecutively
For the operation of reading data (transmitted through data lines) in the SD protocol command, the following
configuration is required:
1) Initialization: Configure the R16_EMMC_CONTROL register to set the sampling edges for commands and
data, the data bus width for transmission and reception, and enable DMA functionality. Configure the
RB_EMMC_TOCNT_MASK bit in the R8_EMMC_TIMEOUT register to set the command timeout and data
timeout durations. Configure the R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1 register to set the DMA start address for storing
read data. Configure the R32_EMMC_BLOCK_CFG register to set the single data block length during transfer
and the total number of data blocks to be read. Configure the R32_EMMC_TRAN_MODE register to set the
DMA transfer direction to “SD to Controller.” Optionally configure whether to automatically stop the clock
during block transfer intervals, allowing sufficient time for application code to perform processing tasks before
software resumes the transfer.
2) Send commands to the SDIO slave interface device. These commands instruct the slave device to transmit data
from the data bus to the host interface, such as CMD17 and CMD18 in the SD protocol.
3) The controller interface reads data from the data line: After the slave interface device responds to the host
command, if the device is ready for data transfer, it outputs data from the data line based on the host clock
signal, with the start signal being a low level. The host controller samples the signal and transfers it via internal
DMA to the user-configured SRAM region. Each transfer of data set by RB_EMMC_BKSIZE_MASK indicates
V1.8 727

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
completion of one data block. Simultaneously, the internal total number of transferred data blocks is
decremented by one. Once all data blocks are transferred, the internal DMA ceases further data transfers. During
this process, the hardware sets the RB_EMMC_IF_BKGAP flag upon completing each data block read. When
all data blocks are read, the hardware sets the RB_EMMC_IF_TRANDONE flag. If a data timeout occurs
during the controller's receive wait period or a CRC error is detected in the received data, the
RB_EMMC_IF_DATTMO and RB_EMMC_IF_TRANERR flags are set respectively. Application code can
configure the corresponding interrupt control bits in the interrupt enable register R16_EMMC_INT_EN. When
the corresponding interrupt flag is set, it triggers the EMMC interrupt service routine.
4) Detection Status: The R32_EMMC_STATUS register enables real-time monitoring of the logic levels on data
line MD0 and command line MCMD. It evaluates these levels according to protocol-defined timing
specifications. The MASK_BLOCK_NUM field records the number of data blocks successfully transferred via
DMA during the current command transmission.
33.2.4 Write Multiple Data Blocks Consecutively
1) Configure the R16_EMMC_CONTROL register to set the sampling edges for commands and data, the data bus
width for transmission and reception, and enable DMA functionality. Configure the
RB_EMMC_TOCNT_MASK bit in the R8_EMMC_TIMEOUT register to set the command timeout and data
timeout durations. After successful command transmission, configure the R32_EMMC_BLOCK_CFG register
to set the single data block length during transfer and the total number of data blocks to be read, thereby
initiating data transfer. Configure the R32_EMMC_TRAN_MODE register to set the DMA transfer direction
to “Controller to SD”.
2) Send commands to the SDIO slave interface device. These commands require the host interface to transmit data
to the slave device via the data cable, such as CMD24 and CMD25 in the SD protocol.
3) The controller interface writes data to the data line: After the slave interface device responds to the host
command, it generates a response packet and releases the data line state (non-low level). At this point, the host
can drive the data line to output a data block. Writing to the DMA register R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1 or
performing a write operation to the R32_EMMC_WRITE_CONT register both trigger the host interface to
drive the data line. The difference lies in the behavior when manipulating register R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1:
the hardware loads the current value of the R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1 register internally and fetches data from
this address to send to the controller. whereas writing to the R32_EMMC_WRITE_CONT register instructs the
hardware to continue fetching SRAM data from the position currently occupied by the DMA internally.
Therefore, to change the DMA address (making it non-contiguous with previous data), the
R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1 register must be rewritten to resume data line output. If the new address is
contiguous with previously written data, the hardware automatically fetches data from the address and moves
it. You can directly write to the R32_EMMC_WRITE_CONT register to instruct the controller to continue data
line output. Each time data of the size specified by RB_EMMC_BKSIZE_MASK is output, it indicates the
completion of one data block transfer. Simultaneously, the internal total number of transferred data blocks is
decremented by one. Once all data blocks have been transferred, the internal DMA will cease further data output.
During this process, upon completing the read of each data block, the hardware sets the
RB_EMMC_IF_BKGAP flag. When all data blocks are read, the hardware sets the
RB_EMMC_IF_TRANDONE flag. If a data timeout occurs during the controller's wait for reception or a CRC
error is detected in the received data, the RB_EMMC_IF_DATTMO and RB_EMMC_IF_TRANERR flags are
set respectively. Application code can configure the corresponding interrupt control bits in the interrupt enable
register R16_EMMC_INT_EN. When the corresponding interrupt flag is set, it triggers the EMMC interrupt
service routine.
V1.8 728

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
Note 1: When the controller interface writes data blocks to external devices, it must wait for command transmission
and acknowledgment completion before setting the DMA address. This is because setting the DMA address notifies
the hardware to drive the data lines; if the command has not yet finished transmitting at this point, the device will
not accept the data.
Note 2: During a transmission process (including data read and write) for a given command execution, if a CRC
error (RB_EMMC_IF_TRANERR) occurs, the hardware will not count it as a successful transmission and will not
decrement the total transmission block count. It will proceed to transmit the next block. However, DMA will still
place the data block containing this CRC error into the corresponding SRAM address area. Application code must
handle this situation appropriately.
33.2.5 DMA Dual-buffer Function
The system provides DMA dual-buffering functionality, featuring two DMA address registers:
R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1 and R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG2, along with the data block length threshold
RB_EMMC_DMATN_CNT for DMA switching. When the data block length threshold starting from the
R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1 register address completes transmission, the hardware switches to the address range set
by R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG2 for data transfer. Upon reaching the transfer threshold, it cycles back to the
R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1 range. This process repeats until all data blocks configured by
RB_EMMC_BKNUM_MASK are fully transferred.
Each time non-zero data is written to the RB_EMMC_BKNUM_MASK field of the R32_EMMC_BLOCK_CFG
register, a data transfer is initiated. Concurrently, the hardware directs DMA operations to the address range starting
at R32_EMMC_DMA_BEG1. The flag-setting conditions during the transfer process remain consistent with the
previously described behavior. Application code may optionally enable the corresponding interrupt flag to trigger
the EMMC interrupt service routine.
33.2.6 Slave Mode
Slave mode operation
The hardware in slave mode only supports R1-type responses, so the R16_EMMC_CMD_SET register has no effect
in slave mode.
1) Host queries slave data status:
The slave device pre-populates the ARGUMENT register with its desired data reception/transmission status. The
host sends CMD13 to query the slave's status and determines whether to read or write to the slave based on the
response.
Note: The use of CMD13 and the bit definitions in the slave's response are software-defined.
2) Host sends CMD18 to read multiple blocks:
The CMD18 command parameter from the host no longer specifies a sector address but instead indicates the number
of blocks to be read in this operation. Upon receiving the command interrupt, the slave configures the DMA address,
sets the R32_EMMC_TRAN_MODE, reads the block count from the command parameter register, and writes it
into the R32_EMMC_BLOCK_CFG register.
2) Host sends CMD25 to write multiple blocks:
The CMD25 command parameter from the host no longer specifies a sector address but instead indicates the number
of blocks to be written in this operation. Upon receiving the command interrupt, the slave configures the DMA
address and sets R32_EMMC_TRAN_MODE. It then reads the block count from the command parameter register
and writes it into the R32_EMMC_BLOCK_CFG register.
Slave error processing
V1.8 729

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
The slave responds to host commands with an R1-type acknowledgment, where the response parameter is the value
of the slave's ARGUMENT register. If the slave fails to acknowledge the host due to a CRC error during command
reception, the host should retry the current command.
If the slave experiences an internal FIFO overflow during transmission or reception, the hardware automatically
forces the current data block to be CRC-erroneous, signaling transmission issues to the host. Alternatively, software
can set RB_SLV_FORCE_ERR to force transmission of the erroneous CRC block.
The slave hardware parses a special command, CMD63, to simplify the slave software's handling of transmission
errors. If a CRC error occurs during host transmission or reception, the host immediately sends CMD63. Upon
receiving CMD63, the slave software must reset the data state machine. The hardware automatically sets the DMA
address to the starting address of the previous erroneous packet. Once master-slave negotiation resumes
transmission, for read operations, the slave software only needs to set the block count in
R32_EMMC_BLOCK_CFG. For write operations, the software configures the block count in
R32_EMMC_BLOCK_CFG and writes to the RESPONSE3 register to complete retransmission and resume data
transfer.
Dual buffer mode
If the slave operates in dual-buffered mode, and an error occurs while the master reads the last block of data from
buf0, the master will send CMD63 during the transmission of the first block of buf1 to indicate a CRC error in the
previous packet. Therefore, the slave should only update the data in buf0 after the first block of buf1 has been
successfully transmitted. The newly added interrupt bit RB_SIF_SLV_BUF_RELEASE is generated when the first
sector of the new buffer is successfully transmitted.

DDR mode
Support DDR mode under 4-wire and 8-wire.
1) 4-wire DDR mode:
That is, through the rising edge and falling edge of the clock, data is output and sampled to improve the data
transmission rate. When applied, 4-wire mode register and DDR mode register should be enabled.

The R32_EMMC_RESPONSE3 register is multiplexed. This multiplexing occurs as follows: When using the CMD25
command to write multiple blocks of data to the card consecutively, writing to this register upon completion of a
block transfer causes the controller to automatically offset the address by the block length and continue writing
data. If the DMA address needs to be changed, writing the DMA address register will initiate the write operation,
eliminating the need to use register writes for initiation.

Chapter 34 Programmable Protocol I/O Microcontroller (PIOC)
A programmable protocol I/O microcontroller is embedded in the chip. The microcontroller is based on the RISC
core with a single clock cycle, runs at the main frequency of the system, has a program ROM with 2K instructions,
49 SFR registers and PWM timers/counters, and supports the protocol control of two I/O pins.
34.1 Main Features
 RISC core, optimized single cycle bit manipulation instruction set, fully static design.
 Multiplex 4K bytes of system SRAM as 2K capacity program ROM, supports program pause and dynamic
loading.
 Provide 33 bytes of 1 register each in bidirectional and unidirectional mode, providing 6 levels of independent
stacking.
 Support 2 general-purpose bi-directional I/O protocol controls and input level change detection.
 Support 1- and 2-wire interfaces with multiple protocol specifications by dynamically loading different
protocol programs.
 Support 1-wire ARGB chip 1024-stage series connection
34.2 Instruction, Program Space and Stack
34.2.1 Instruction Set
eMCU adopts RISC8B core with reduced instruction set, with data width of 8 bits and instruction width of 16 bits.
There are 66 instructions, all of which are single clock cycles, except that the jump instruction is double clock cycle
and the program space reading and writing instruction is double cycle. For more information, please refer to RISC8B
core instruction set and assembly tool document CHRISC8B.PDF.
34.2.2 Program ROM
EMCU's program ROM comes from 4-kbyte system SRAM multiplexing. When SB_MST_CLK_GATE is 0, it is
dedicated to the system SRAM on the host side, and when SB_MST_CLK_GATE is 1, it is dedicated to eMCU's
program ROM.
The program space of eMCU is 2048 words, and the address of the program space ranges from 0x0000 to 0x07FF.
The instruction at address 0 in the program ROM has a special purpose and will not be executed.
eMCU chip supports reading program space. The steps are as follows: first, write the lower 8 bits of the target
address into SFR_INDIR_ADDR, and the upper 3 bits of the target address into the A register, and then execute the
RDCODE instruction, so that the 16-bit data in the program space can be read out at one time, which is divided into
high and low bytes, with the low byte returned to the A register and the high byte returned to the
SFR_INDIR_ADDR. This operation can be used for double-byte table lookup.
eMCU chip does not support writing to program space.
34.2.3 Stack
The eMCU features a stack memory with a depth of 6 levels and an 11-bit data width. It is used to store the program
return address during subroutine calls and can also be employed with the PUSHAS instruction to save variables,
status data, and other information from the running program onto the stack.
V1.8 743

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
34.2.4 Sleep and Awakening
When SB_MST_CLK_GATE is 0, the eMCU program will suspend execution. After executing the SLEEP or
SLEEPX instruction, the eMCU enters sleep mode. The eMCU is designed as fully static, where program suspension
and sleep mode have equivalent effects.
After entering sleep, the eMCU supports two wake-up methods: - Wake-up via level change on a pin with level
change detection enabled. - Wake-up via the SB_MST_CLK_GATE signal conversioning from 0 to 1.
34.2.5 Event Wait Instruction
The WAITB instruction supports waiting for 8 types of events. When the event is invalid, WAITB continues to wait
indefinitely, with the program counter (PC) remaining unchanged. Upon detecting the target event, the wait is
terminated, and the next instruction is executed. Timer timeout reset can be optionally enabled during the wait.
The instruction parameter WB_DATA_SW_MR_0 indicates waiting until SB_DATA_SW_MR becomes 0 to exit;
if it is already 0, exit immediately.
The instruction parameter WB_BIT_CYC_TAIL_1 indicates waiting until SB_BIT_CYC_TAIL becomes 1 to exit;
if it is already 1, it exits immediately.
The instruction parameter WB_PORT_I0_FALL indicates waiting until SB_PORT_IN0 detects a falling edge to
exit; if a falling edge was previously detected and recorded, it also exits immediately, clearing the falling edge
detection record upon exit.
The instruction parameter WB_PORT_I0_RISE indicates waiting until SB_PORT_IN0 detects a rising edge to exit.
If a rising edge has already been detected as recorded, it exits directly and clears the rising edge detection record
upon exit.
The instruction parameter WB_DATA_MW_SR_1 indicates waiting until SB_DATA_MW_SR is 1 to exit. If it is
already 1, it exits directly.
The instruction parameter WB_PORT_XOR1_1 indicates waiting until SB_PORT_XOR1 is 1 before exiting. If it
is already 1, exit directly.
The instruction parameter WB_PORT_XOR0_0 indicates waiting until SB_PORT_XOR0 is 0 before exiting. If it
is already 0, exit directly.
The instruction parameter WB_PORT_XOR0_1 indicates waiting until SB_PORT_XOR0 is 1 before exiting; if it
is already 1, exit immediately.
34.2.6 Bit Transfer Instruction
Bit transfer instructions support two bit operation registers: BP1F and BG1F correspond to register
SFR_INDIR_ADDR, while BP2F and BG2F correspond to register SFR_DATA_EXCH.
Bit transfer instructions BP1F and BP2F support four independent bit outputs: Parameter 0# BIO_FLAG_C
corresponds to SB_FLAG_C bit, parameter 1# BO_BIT_TX_O0 corresponds to SB_BIT_TX_O0, parameter 2#
BO_PORT_OUT0 corresponds to SB_PORT_OUT0, and parameter 3# BO_PORT_OUT1 corresponds to
SB_PORT_OUT1.
Bit transfer instructions BG1F and BG2F support four independent bit inputs: Parameter 0# (BIO_FLAG_C)
corresponds to bit SB_FLAG_C, parameter 1# (BI_BIT_RX_I0) corresponds to bit SB_BIT_RX_I0, parameter 2#
(BI_PORT_IN0) corresponds to bit SB_PORT_IN0, and parameter 3# (BI_PORT_IN1) corresponds to bit
SB_PORT_IN1.
The bit transfer instruction BCTC supports four independent bit inputs: Parameter 0# BI_C_XOR_IN0 updates bit
SB_FLAG_C to the XOR result of SB_FLAG_C and SB_PORT_IN0; Parameter 1# BI_BIT_RX_I0 corresponds
to SB_BIT_RX_I0; Parameter 2# BI_PORT_IN0 corresponds to SB_PORT_IN0; Parameter 3# BI_PORT_IN1
V1.8 744

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
corresponds to SB_PORT_IN1.
34.3 Data Space and Registers and Addressing
The data space of the eMCU includes 49 dedicated special function registers (SFRs) addressed via 8-bit addresses
within the range 0x00 to 0x3F. All registers have a data width of 1 byte, equivalent to 8 bits.
Some SFRs are accessible for read/write or read-only operations from the host side, which supports 8-bit, 16-bit, or
32-bit width read/write operations. The host side has write priority. When both the eMCU and host attempt to write
to the same register simultaneously, the eMCU's write operation is automatically discarded.
The eMCU's addressing modes include: immediate address, immediate fast address, standard direct address,
extended direct address, indirect address, and bit address. The latter four are used for register addressing.
The indirect addressing range is 0x000-0x0FF, covering all registers of the eMCU. The eMCU provides two sets of
indirect address registers, each consisting of an address register and a data read/write port. First, write the target
register's address into the address register, then read or write the target register via the data read/write port.
The address range for extended direct addressing is 0x000-0x1FF, where the instruction directly provides a 9-bit
register address. This is only applicable to the following two direct register read/write instructions: MOV register,A
or F, and MOVA register.
The addressing range for standard direct addressing is 0x000-0x0FF. The instruction directly provides an 8-bit
register address, applicable to all direct address instructions except those covered by extended direct addressing,
such as CLR register, ADD register, BS register, bit, etc. When addressing a larger range is required, indirect
addressing should be employed.
Immediate number fast addressing enables rapid writing of operands from instruction codes to target registers
without requiring an A register intermediary. MOVA1F is used for fast setting of register #1 (SFR_PORT_DIR),
while MOVA2F is used for fast setting of register #2 (SFR_PORT_IO). MOVA1P and MOVA2P employ indirect
addressing for rapid setting of all registers, equivalent to first performing immediate addressing followed by indirect
addressing within a single cycle.
Bit addressing utilizes a 3-bit address provided directly by the instruction. Register addressing can employ either
standard direct addressing or indirect addressing, covering address ranges 0x000 to 0x0FF respectively, thereby
enabling access to any bit within any register.

The default values after reset are all represented by binary numbers, and the bit values are described as follows:
0: Always 0 after reset;
1: Always 1 after reset;
X: Reset does not affect data; initial data value is undefined;
-: Always clears to 0 after power-on reset; system reset or host forced reset does not affect data.
The read/write specifications for the host side are as follows:
W: Bits that can be read or written;
R: Read-only bits;
U: Invisible bit, neither readable nor writable;
S: Read-only switch bit. The host-side visible SFR_TIMER_CTRL differs from the eMCU side in that the
SB_TMR0_ENABLE and SB_TMR0_OUT_EN bits are replaced by SB_GP_BIT_Y and SB_GP_BIT_X
respectively.
34.4.1 Indirect Addressed Data Read-write Port (SFR_INDIR_PORT)
34.4.2 Address Register of Indirect Addressed (SFR_INDIR_ADDR)
34.4.3 Indirect Addressed 2 Data Read-write Port (SFR_INDIR_PORT2)
34.4.4 Address Register of Indirect Addressed 2 (SFR_INDIR_ADDR2)
These are 2 sets of indirect address registers, each consisting of an address register and a data read/write port. First,
write the destination register's address into the address register. Then, read or write the destination register by
V1.8 747

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
accessing the data read/write port.
The data read/write port SFR_INDIR_PORT for indirect addressing reads/writes the destination register specified
by the indirectly addressed address register SFR_INDIR_ADDR. The data read/write port SFR_INDIR_PORT2 for
indirect addressing reads/writes the destination register specified by the indirectly addressed address register
SFR_INDIR_ADDR2.
The dedicated instruction MOVIP is used to load an 8-bit destination address into SFR_INDIR_ADDR. Additionally,
SFR_INDIR_ADDR can be modified independently by other non-dedicated instructions.
The dedicated instruction MOVIA is used to load an 8-bit target address into SFR_INDIR_ADDR2, and
SFR_INDIR_ADDR2 can also be independently modified by other non-dedicated instructions.
The address register SFR_INDIR_ADDR2 for Indirect Addressing Mode 2 features automatic incrementing. When
executing the “MOV SFR_INDIR_PORT2,A” read instruction or the “MOVA SFR_INDIR_PORT2” write
instruction to RAM, SFR_INDIR_ADDR2 will automatically increment by 1 upon instruction completion.
The dedicated instructions MOVA1P and MOVA2P are used to directly and rapidly write operands from the
instruction code into target registers, equivalent to performing immediate addressing followed by indirect addressing
within a single cycle.
34.4.5 Status Register (SFR_STATUS_REG)
The status register contains the result status of the ALU, general-purpose bit variables, and stack usage flags. After
executing arithmetic or logical operations, the eMCU sets corresponding status bits based on the results, enabling
the program to make judgments and perform further processing. General-purpose bit variables can be defined for
specific purposes by the application.
The timer timeout reset monitors the timeout of WAITB wait instructions. After disabling SB_TMR0_ENABLE
and enabling SB_EN_TOUT_RST, the timer counts during WAITB execution. When overflow occurs and
SB_TMR0_CYCLE is 1, a timeout reset is triggered. The timer initial value is automatically reloaded each time the
WAITB instruction exits the WAITB wait state upon condition fulfillment. Counting does not occur during
execution of non-WAITB instructions when SB_TMR0_ENABLE is 0, meaning the timer timeout reset applies
exclusively to the WAITB instruction.

34.4.6 Low Byte of Program Counter PC (SFR_PRG_COUNT)
The program counter (PC) of the eMCU is 11 bits wide. The lower 8 bits of the PC can be modified by reading or
writing SFR_PRG_COUNT, but this does not affect the upper 3 bits. This allows for short jumps and lookup table
operations within a 256-byte range.

34.4.8 Port Input Output Register (SFR_PORT_IO)
The port contains two bidirectional input/output pins, each independently configurable as input or output via its
respective direction bit SB_PORT_DIR. When set as output, data from SB_PORT_OUT is output to the pin. The
default direction after reset is input. SB_PORT_IN is used to acquire the current pin input level (when
SB_PORT_IN_EDGE=0) or the pin input level from the previous cycle (when SB_PORT_IN_EDGE=1), with the
latter being approximately half a clock cycle ahead of the former.

34.4.9 Count Register of Timer 0 (SFR_TMR0_COUNT)
34.4.10 Initial Value Register of Timer 0 (SFR_TMR0_INIT)
34.4.11 Control Register of Timer (SFR_TIMER_CTRL)
Timer 0 is an 8-bit counter. The count value is stored in the SFR_TMR0_COUNT register, which supports direct
data write to load new values. The clock frequency for Timer 0 is selected via SB_TMR0_FREQ. Timer 0 can
operate in either timer mode or pulse width modulator (PWM) mode.
In timer mode, Timer 0's initial count value is stored in advance in the initial value register SFR_TMR0_INIT. Timer
0 always counts from this initial value up to 0FFH. Upon overflowing from 0FFH, Timer 0 automatically reloads
V1.8 750

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
the initial value from the initial value register SFR_TMR0_INIT and begins counting from the initial value toward
0FFH again. When counting from 0FEH to 0FFH, Timer 0 automatically sets the cycle signal SB_TMR0_CYCLE
to 1. When counting overflows from 0FFH back to the initial value, Timer 0 automatically clears the cycle signal
SB_TMR0_CYCLE to 0. The frequency of SB_TMR0_CYCLE is (SB_TMR0_FREQ clock frequency) / (256 -
SFR_TMR0_INIT), with a duty cycle of 1 / (256 - SFR_TMR0_INIT). This means SB_TMR0_CYCLE is active
for one clock cycle per period.
In pulse width modulator mode, Timer 0 always counts from 00H to 0FFH, then overflows from 0FFH and resets
to 00H to begin a new count cycle. Its period is always 256 clock cycles. When the count value exceeds the value
stored in the Timer 0 initialization register (SFR_TMR0_INIT), Timer 0 automatically sets the cycle signal
SB_TMR0_CYCLE to 1. When the count value overflows from 0FFH back to 00H, Timer 0 automatically clears
the cycle signal SB_TMR0_CYCLE to 0. The duty cycle of SB_TMR0_CYCLE is (255 - SFR_TMR0_INIT) / 256.
SB_TMR0_OUT_EN determines whether the internal signal SB_TMR0_CYCLE or its 2-division signal is output
to the IO0 pin. When the internal signal is high, the pin outputs a high level; otherwise, it outputs a low level. If the
cycle signal output is enabled, then in timer mode, the 2-division signal of SB_TMR0_CYCLE (reduced to half
frequency with a 50% duty cycle) will be output through the IO0 pin; in pulse width modulator mode, the
SB_TMR0_CYCLE signal will be output through the IO0 pin.

34.4.12 System Configuration Register (SFR_SYS_CFG)
34.4.13 Host Reads and Writes and eMCU Read-only Register (SFR_CTRL_WR)
34.4.14 System Configuration Register (SFR_CTRL_RD)
The System Configuration Register provides control bits for the host and status bits for bidirectional data exchange.
SB_INT_REQ is fully controlled by the eMCU to request interrupts or cancel requests to the host. However, the
host can clear SB_INT_REQ to 0 by performing a dummy write operation to the read-only register SFR_CTRL_RD.
Writing to SFR_CTRL_RD has no practical effect on its data.
After the eMCU writes to SFR_CTRL_RD, SB_DATA_SW_MR is automatically set to 1. After the host reads
SFR_CTRL_RD, SB_DATA_SW_MR is automatically cleared to 0.
After the host writes to SFR_CTRL_WR, SB_DATA_MW_SR is automatically set to 1. After the eMCU reads
SFR_CTRL_WR, SB_DATA_MW_SR is automatically cleared to 0.
SB_MST_CLK_GATE also controls the multiplexing of the eMCU program ROM. When SB_MST_CLK_GATE
is 0, it is dedicated to the host-side system SRAM, totaling 4K bytes, enabling dynamic loading of new programs
for the eMCU. When SB_MST_CLK_GATE is 1, it is dedicated to the eMCU program ROM, containing 2K
instructions.
Bits 0 to 4 of the system configuration register are fully controlled by the host and are read-only on the eMCU side.

34.4.15 Coded Bit Period Register (SFR_BIT_CYCLE)
34.4.16 Coded Bit Configuration Register (SFR_BIT_CONFIG)
The eMCU supports 2 bit-modulation methods: PWM duty cycle modulation and Manchester modulation.
Setting SB_BIT_CYCLE greater than 3 enables encoding/decoding. When SB_BIT_TX_EN=0, the system receives
data. Input status is received from IO0 based on the preset width, and decoded data is stored in SB_BIT_RX_I0.
When SB_BIT_TX_EN=1, the system transmits data. Raw data to be transmitted is placed in SB_BIT_TX_O0.
After encoding, it is automatically delivered to SB_PORT_OUT0 for pin output.
SB_BIT_CYC_CNT and SB_BIT_CYC_TAIL indicate the cycle status of the encoded bit. When
SB_BIT_CYC_TAIL=1, it signifies the current phase is within the last 25% of the bit cycle, indicating that
SB_BIT_RX_I0 has completed reception and decoding, and the transmission encoding is finished and has reached
SB_PORT_OUT0.
Setting SB_BIT_CYCLE=0 forces SB_BIT_CYC_TAIL to 1, facilitating Manchester encoding/decoding initiation.
Setting SFR_BIT_CYCLE clears the rising and falling edge detection records for IO0, enabling the WAITB
instruction to restart waiting.

0: Sample at the midpoint of the current clock cycle, offering
relatively higher real-time performance.

34.4.17 Data Register (SFR_DATA_x) (x=0-31)
SFR_DATA_x are all bidirectional read/write data registers. Write operations from the host take precedence, and
their functions are software-defined.
Among these, SFR_DATA_EXCH also supports single-cycle bit transfer instructions.
34.5 Application
The eMCU operates at the same clock frequency as the host side, facilitating dynamic data exchange. It features a
rich set of bit manipulation instructions, enabling single-cycle I/O configuration, single-cycle I/O status polling, or
bit data copying. It supports hardware encoding/decoding of PWM or Manchester-modulated bit data, making it
suitable for implementing I/O for various low-to-medium speed communication protocols and for I/O control
requiring precise timing.
V1.8 754

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
Chapter 35 Operational Amplifier (OPA) and Comparator (CMP)
The module consists of 3 independently configurable operational amplifier (OPA1/OPA2/OPA3) and 1
independently configurable voltage comparator (CMP). The operational amplifier (OPA) supports gain selection or
can be used as a voltage comparator.
The input and output of each operational amplifier are connected to the I/O port, and the input pin or gain is optional,
and the output pin can be optionally configured to the universal I/O port or multiplexed as an ADC sampling channel.
The external analog small signal is amplified into the ADC to achieve small-signal ADC conversion.
The input and output of each voltage comparator are connected to the I/O port, and the input pins are optional, and
the output pins can be optionally configured to the universal I/O port or multiplexed as an TIM internal sampling
channel (without using the I/O pin).
35.1 Main Features
 OPA input pin/output channel can be selected.
 OPA1 output channel directly connected to comparator input
 OPA supports voltage buffer (BUFFER) and programmable gain amplifier (PGA)
 CMP input pin selectable
 CMP positive input supports selectable DAC output; negative input supports selectable internal self-bias
voltage
 CMP supports selectable digital filtering and hysteresis
 CMP output pin selectable as general-purpose I/O port or TIM internal sampling channel
35.2 Function Description
35.2.1 OPA1/OPA2/OPA3
OPA1, OPA2, and OPA3 support voltage buffers (BUFFER) and programmable gain amplifiers (PGA). As shown
in Figure 35-1, these 3 OPAs share essentially identical functionality. Compared to OPA2 and OPA3, OPA1 features
an additional output channel connected to the CMP_P2 input of the voltage comparator.
In the R32_OPA_CTLR1 register: Setting the EN1 bit enables OPA1; Setting the PSEL1 bit selects the positive
input channel for OPA1; Setting the NSEL1 bit selects the negative input channel for OPA1 or enables PGA mode
to configure the internal gain of OPA1. Configuring the FB_EN1 bit enables the PGA mode feedback for OPA1.
Configuring the PGADIF1 bit enables the differential input PGA mode, allowing OPA1 to function as a PGA in
conjunction with NSEL1, with the N terminal connected to PA7. Configuring the HS1 bit enables high-speed mode,
which improves slew rate in this mode. Configuring the MODE1[1:0] bits selects the output channel as either a
GPIO or the positive input of a comparator.
In the R32_OPA_CTLR2 register: Setting the EN2 bit enables OPA2; Setting the PSEL2 bit selects the positive
input channel for OPA2; Setting the NSEL2 bit selects the negative input channel for OPA2 or enables PGA mode
to configure the internal gain of OPA2. Configure the FB_EN2 bit to enable OPA2's PGA mode feedback; configure
the PGADIF2 bit to enable differential input PGA mode, allowing OPA2 to function as a PGA with NSEL2 set, with
the N terminal connected to PF12; configure the HS2 bit to enable high-speed mode, which improves slew rate in
this mode; configure the MODE2 bit to select the output channel.
V1.8 755

CH32H417 Reference Manual                                          https://wch-ic.com
In the R32_OPA_CTLR3 register: Configure the EN3 bit to enable OPA3; Configure the PSEL3 bit to select the
positive input channel for OPA3; Configure the NSEL3 bit to select the negative input channel for OPA3 or enable
PGA mode, setting the internal gain of OPA3. Configure the FB_EN3 bit to enable OPA3's PGA mode feedback.
Configure the PGADIF3 bit to enable differential input PGA mode, allowing OPA3 to function as a PGA with
NSEL3 set, with the N terminal connected to PA3. Configure the HS3 bit to enable high-speed mode, which
improves slew rate in this mode. Configure the MODE3 bit to select the output channel.

35.2.2 CMP
CMP supports optional hysteresis characteristics, digital filtering at the output, and optional output filtering. The
structure diagram is shown in Figure 35-2.
V1.8                                              756

CH32H417 Reference Manual                                          https://wch-ic.com
In the R32_CMP_CTLR register: Configure the EN bit to enable the CMP module; Configure the PSEL[1:0] bits
to select whether the P-channel is connected to a GPIO input or internally linked to the OPA operational amplifier;
Configure the NSEL[1:0] bits to select whether the N-channel is connected to a GPIO input, internally linked to the
DAC output, or connected to an optional internal self-bias voltage. Configure the HYPSEL bit to select the
comparator hysteresis voltage; configure the VREF bit to select the CMP internal bias voltage magnitude; configure
the FILT_EN bit to enable the CMP output digital filtering function; configure the FILT_CFG[8:0] bits to select the
CMP output digital filtering sampling interval, which must be greater than the noise width and less than twice the
noise width; Configure the FILT_BASE[2:0] bits to set the time reference for the CMP output digital filter sampling.
Configure the MODE[3:0] bits to select whether the CMP2 output connects internally to the I/O or connects to the
timer break input/internal sampling channel of the timer.
In the R32_CMP_STATR register, the output result of CMP filtering function closing/opening can be read through
the OUT_FILT bit.

Chapter 36 Serial Audio Interface (SAI)
Serial Audio Interface (SAI) supports various common audio protocols, such as I2S, PCM/DSP, AC'97, LSB or
MSB alignment and TDM, which is suitable for mono and stereo applications. In order to realize the flexibility and
configurability of SAI interface, it adopts two completely independent audio submodules, each of which contains
up to four IO pins (SD, SCK, FS and MCLK).
SAI can be configured as any combination of master/slave and sending/receiving, and its operation mode can be set
as full duplex/simplex according to the synchronous/asynchronous configuration of audio submodule.
36.1 Main Features
 Provide 2 independent control modules, with each audio submodule configurable in any combination of
master/slave or transmit/receive roles, each featuring an 8-word FIFO
 Audio submodules can operate in synchronous or asynchronous modes, with master/slave configurations
independent of each other
 Flexible slot length configuration, with slots configurable as valid or invalid
 Frame synchronization configuration (valid level, valid length, and offset)
 Each audio frame contains up to 16 configurable slots
 Up to 16 slots, each supporting 8-bit, 10-bit, 16-bit, 20-bit, 24-bit, or 32-bit data
 Support LSB or MSB data transmission
 Support multiple audio protocols including I2S standard, LSB or MSB alignment, PCM/DSP, TDM, and AC'97
 Features mono/stereo audio functionality with mute settings
 Serial clock strobe edge selection (SCK)
 Each audio submodule has 2 independent DMA interfaces
 Error flag bits and interrupt sources:
- FIFO overflow and underflow;
- Frame sync advance detection in slave mode;
- Frame sync lag detection in slave mode;
- AC'97 codec not ready;
- Clock configuration error.

HB Interface
The SAI primarily consists of 2 independent audio submodules connected to the output via an I/O management
module. The I/O line controller manages four dedicated pins (SD, SCK, FS, MCLK) for the specified audio module
within the SAI. If both submodules are declared as synchronous modules, certain pins can be shared, freeing others
for use as general-purpose I/O. Whether the MCLK pin can function as an output pin depends on the specific
application and decoding requirements, as well as whether the audio module is configured in master mode.
Each audio module integrates a 32-bit shift register controlled by the module's own functional state machine. Data
storage and retrieval are performed via dedicated FIFOs. These FIFOs can be accessed by the CPU or via DMA to
reduce the CPU's communication load.
The audio submodule can function as either a transmitter or receiver in both master and slave modes. Master mode
indicates that the SAI generates the SCK bit clock and frame synchronizing signal, while slave mode indicates that
the SCK bit clock and frame synchronizing signal originate from another external or internal master device. In
specific cases, the direction of the FS signal is not directly related to the master or slave mode definition. Within the
AC'97 protocol, even when the SAI (link controller) is configured to consume the SCK clock, the FS signal remains
an SAI output (this also applies in slave mode).
36.3 Function Description
36.3.1 Clock Generator
Both independent audio submodules of the SAI have their own clock generators, but these clock generators function
identically.
When the audio module is configured in master mode, the clock generator provides the bit clock (SCK) and the
master clock (MCLK) for the external decoder. When the audio module is defined as slave mode, the clock generator
is disabled.

CH32H417 Reference Manual                                          https://wch-ic.com
The bit clock strobe edge on SCK can be configured via the CKSTR bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register. This bit
applies to both master and slave modes.
It is recommended to select the PLL output of 295MHz as the input clock for the SAI.
The architecture of the audio module clock generator is shown in Figure 36-2.

The clock source of the clock generator comes from the product clock controller. SAI_CK_x clock is equivalent to
the master clock, and can divide the frequency for the external decoder through MCKDIV[5:0] bits:
If MCKDIV[5:0] is not equal to 0000b, then MCLK_x = SAI_CK_x / (MCKDIV[5:0] * 2)
If MCKDIV[5:0] is equal to 0000b, then MCLK_x = SAI_CK_x

Frequency division must be uniform to maintain a 50% duty cycle on both the MCLK output and the SCK clock. If
the MCKDIV[5:0] bits are set to 0000b, a single division ratio is used to make MCLK equal to SAI_CK_x.
In the SAI, a single ratio MCLK/FS = 256 is used. In most cases, three frequency ranges will be encountered, as

If the corresponding audio module is configured as the master module and the NODIV bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1
register is set to 0, the master clock can be generated for an external decoder via the I/O port. When the audio
module is defined as slave mode, the clock generator is disabled. The values of the NODIV and MCKDIV bits are
V1.8                                              765

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
ignored. Additionally, the MCLK I/O pin is released and can be used as a general-purpose I/O.
The bit clock is derived from the master clock. The bit clock divider sets the division factor between the bit clock
(SCK) and the master clock (SCK) according to the following formula:
SCK = MCLK*(FRL[7:0]+1)/256
Among them:
256 is the fixed ratio between MCLK and the audio sampling frequency;
FRL[7:0] represents the number of bit clock cycles within an audio frame minus one, configured in the
R32_SAI_xFRCR register.
In Master Mode, (FRL[7:0]+1) must equal a power of 2 to yield an even number of MCLK pulses per bit clock
cycle. A 50% duty cycle is guaranteed on the bit clock (SCK).
The SAI_CK_x clock may also equal the bit clock frequency. In this case, the NODIV bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1
register should be set to 1, and the values within the MCKDIV divider and the bit clock divider will be ignored. At
this time, the number of bits in each frame is completely configurable, and it is not necessary to be equal to several
powers of 2.
36.3.2 Operation Mode
The SAI audio submodule can be configured via the MODE[1:0] bits of the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register to operate
in any combination of master/slave, transmit/receive modes.
Each audio module within the SAI is enabled via the SAIEN bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register. In slave mode,
once this bit is activated, the transmitter or receiver becomes sensitive to activity on the clock line, data line, and
sync line.
In master TX mode, the enabled audio module immediately generates bit clocks for the external slave module even
if no data is present in the FIFO, but the generation of the FS signal is controlled by the presence of data in the FIFO.
Upon receiving the first data to be transmitted, the FIFO outputs this data to the external slave module. If no data is
present in the FIFO for transmission, subsequent values of zero are transmitted within the audio frame, and an
underflow flag is generated.
In slave mode, audio frames commence when the audio module is enabled and the SOF bit is detected.
In slave TX mode, an underflow event cannot occur on the first frame after enabling the audio module, as the forced
operation sequence is as follows:
1) Write to R32_SAI_xDATAR via software or DMA;
2) Wait until the FIFO threshold (FLTH) flag differs from 000b (indicating FIFO is empty);
3) Enable the audio module for slave transmit mode.
Master mode
In master mode, the SAI provides clock signals to connected external devices:
1) Bit clock and frame sync are output on pins SCK and FS, respectively;
2) If required, the SAI can also generate the master clock on the MCLK pin.
FS is generated when the FIFO is not empty and at the start of a frame. CK and MCLK generation, however, are
not dependent on the FIFO status and are produced whenever the audio submodule is enabled.
Slave mode
In slave mode, the SAI receives clock signals from external devices:
1) When the SAI submodule is configured for asynchronous mode, the SCK and FS pins are configured as inputs.
V1.8 766

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
2) If the SAI submodule is configured to operate synchronously with the second audio submodule, the
corresponding SCK and FS pins are released for use as general-purpose I/O.
In slave mode, the MCLK pin is not used and can be assigned to other functions. It is recommended to enable the
slave device before enabling the master device.
36.3.3 Internal Synchronization Mode
The audio submodule can run synchronously with another audio submodule in the same SAI, which is also called
internal synchronization mode. In this case, they will share the bit clock and frame synchronization signal to reduce
the number of external pins occupied during communication. An audio module configured in synchronous mode
will release its SCK, FS and MCLK pins to be used as GPIO, while an audio module configured in asynchronous
mode will use its SCK, FS and MCLKI/O pins (if the audio module is configured as a master module).
Typically, the audio module in synchronous mode can be used to configure the SAI in full-duplex mode. One of the
two audio modules can be configured as the master module and the other as the slave module; alternatively, both
can be configured as slave modules. One module can be set as the asynchronous module (with the SYNCEN[1:0]
bits in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register set to 00b), and the other as the synchronous module (with the SYNCEN[1:0]
bits in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register set to 01b).
Note: Due to the internal resynchronization phase, the HCLK frequency must be greater than twice the bit rate clock
frequency.
36.3.4 Frame Configuration
36.3.4.1 Frame Synchronization
The FS signal is used as a frame synchronization signal (SOF) in audio. The waveform of this signal can be
completely configurable by configuring R32_SAI_xFRCR register, which can support various audio protocols with
special specifications during frame synchronization. The following figure shows the configurability of audio frames.

R32_SAI_xFRCR register is ignored.
Each audio module operates independently and therefore requires specific configuration.
36.3.4.2 Frame Length
V1.8 767

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
Master mode
Setting the FRL[7:0] field of the R32_SAI_xFRCR register to 1 configures the audio frame length to a maximum
of 256 bit clock cycles.
If the frame length exceeds the number of slots declared for that frame, the remaining bits to be transmitted will
be zero-padded or the SD line will be released to a high configuration, depending on the state of the TRIS bit in
the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register. In receive mode, the remaining bits are ignored.
If the NODIV bit is cleared, (FRL+1) must equal a power of 2 (from 8 to 256) to ensure each bit clock cycle of the
audio frame contains an integer number of MCLK pulses. If the NODIV bit is set to 1, the (FRL+1) field can take
any value from 8 to 256.
Slave mode
The audio frame length is primarily used to specify the number of bit clock cycles for each audio frame
transmitted from the external master module to the slave module. It is mainly employed to detect frame
synchronization signals that occur ahead of schedule or behind schedule during audio frame transmission from the
master module. Errors occur in such cases.
In slave mode, the configuration of the FRL[7:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xFRCR register is unrestricted.
36.3.4.3 Frame Synchronization Polarity
Set the effective polarity of the FS pin through the FSPOL bit in R32_SAI_xFRCR register, and start the frame
through this polarity. SOF signal is sensitive to edge.
In the slave mode, the audio module is in a waiting state until a valid frame signal is received to perform the
sending or receiving operation, and the SOF signal is synchronized with the frame signal. The frame
synchronization polarity is valid only when the SOF signal is not detected during communication and the SOF
signal is consistent with the expected SOF signal.
In the main mode, every time an audio frame is completed, a frame synchronization signal is sent until the SAIEN
bit in the R32_SAI_xCTLR1 register is cleared. If there is no data in the FIFO at the end of the previous audio
frame, the underflow will be handled as described in section 36.3.12.1, but the audio communication flow will not
be interrupted.
36.3.4.4 Frame Synchronization Effective Level Length
The FSALL[6:0] bits of the R32_SAI_xFRCR register configure the length of the active level for the frame sync
signal. This length can be set to between 1 and 128 bit clock cycles.
In I2S, LSB, or MSB alignment modes, the active length is set to half the frame length; in PCM/DSP or TDM
modes, the active length is set to 1 bit.
36.3.4.5 Frame Synchronization Offset
According to the audio protocols supported in the application (such as I2S standard protocol and MSB alignment
protocol), setting the audio frame synchronization offset can make the frame synchronization signal valid when
the last bit or the first bit is transmitted. You can select one of two configurations by using the FSOFF bit in the
R32_SAI_xFRCR register.
36.3.4.6 Function of FS Signal
V1.8 768

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
The meaning of FS signal varies with the function of FS, and the meaning of FS signal can be configured in the
FSDEF bit of R32_SAI_xFRCR register.
- When the FSDEF bit is set to 1, the FS signal simultaneously carries both the SOF signal and channel identification
signal within the frame, suitable for audio frame structures such as I2S, MSB-aligned, or LSB-aligned protocols;
- When the FSDEF bit is set to 0, the FS signal functions as the SOF signal, suitable for PCM/DSP, TDM, AC'97,
and audio protocols.
When interpreting the FS signal as the SOF signal and channel identification signal within a frame, the declared
number of slots should be evenly distributed between the left and right channels. If the number of bit clock cycles
on a half audio frame exceeds the dedicated slot count for a channel and the TRIS bit is set to 0, the remaining bit
clock cycles in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register will output 0. Conversely, if the TRIS bit is set to 1, the SD line will
enter a high-impedance state. During reception, the remaining bit clock cycles are only considered when a channel
change occurs.

36.3.5 Slot Configuration
The basic unit of an audio frame is a Slot, with each audio frame capable of being divided into up to 16 Slots. The
number of Slots within an audio frame is determined by NBSLOT[3:0]+1.
For AC'97 or SPDIF protocols (when PRTCFG[1:0] bits are set to 10b or 01b), the number of Slots is automatically
configured according to the respective protocol specifications, and the value of NBSLOT[3:0] is ignored.
By setting the SLOTEN[15:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xSLOTR register, individual slots can be enabled or disabled.
When transmitting an invalid slot, the SD data line is forcibly set to 0 or placed in a high-impedance state, depending
on the configuration of the TRIS bit in transmit mode (see the section on invalid slot output data line management
for details). In receive mode, data received after the end of this invalid slot is ignored. Consequently, there are no
FIFO accesses, nor any FIFO read/write requests associated with the state of this invalid slot.
Additionally, the slot size can be selected by setting bits SLOTSZ[1:0] in the R32_SAI_xSLOTR register to 1, as
shown in Figure 36-6.
Figure 36-6 Slot size configuration when FBOFF bit 0
The position of the first data bit to be transmitted within the slot, i.e., the offset value of the first bit, can be
configured via the FBOFF[4:0] bits of the R32_SAI_xSLOTR register. As shown in Figure 36-7, in transmit mode,
a value of 0 is injected starting from the Slot's beginning position until the preset offset position is reached. In
V1.8 770

receive mode, bits within the offset phase are ignored. This feature applies to LSB-aligned protocols (if the offset
equals the Slot size minus the data size).
Figure 36-7 First bit offset
To avoid SAI malfunction, the following conditions must be met:
FBOFF ≤ (SLOTSZ - DS),

NBSLOT × SLOTSZ ≤ FRL (Frame Length),
When bit 1 of the R32_SAI_xFRCR register's FSDEF field is set, the number of slots must be even.
In AC'97 and SPDIF protocols (PRTCFG[1:0] bits set to 10b or 01b), slot size is automatically configured
according to Section 36.3.7: AC'97 Link Controller.
36.3.6 Internal FIFO
Each SAI audio submodule contains an independent 8-word-wide synchronous FIFO to enhance transmission
efficiency. These FIFOs can be accessed by either the CPU or DMA, with FIFO request interrupts used to request
CPU and DMA access.
Depending on whether the audio module is defined as a transmitter or receiver, corresponding reads or writes to
the FIFO are executed. Regardless of the access size, each read or write operation to the FIFO operates on a single
word-sized FIFO cell. Each FIFO word contains one audio slot. Following each access to the R32_SAI_xDATAR
register, the FIFO pointer increments by one word. Consequently, only one FIFO request is associated with the
FREQ bit (FIFO request flag) in the R32_SAI_xSR register.
When the FREQIE bit in the R32_SAI_xINTENR register is enabled, an interrupt will be generated. The
triggering conditions for this interrupt depend on the operating mode, FIFO threshold, FIFO status, and DMA
burst transfer size.
The specific interrupt triggering mechanism is detailed in Table 36-2 and the subsequent sections 'Generating
Interrupts in Transmit Mode' and 'Generating Interrupts in Receive Mode'.

Note: (1) If the fundamental conditions are not met, the interrupt request will be cleared by hardware.
(2) After disabling SAI by setting bit 1 of the FFLUSH field in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register, the FIFO
pointer can be reinitialized. If FFLUSH is set to 1 while SAI is enabled, the data in the FIFO will be automatically
cleared, and the read/write pointer will be reset to 0.
Generate an interrupt in send mode
According to the FIFO configuration in transmit mode, an interrupt is generated:
When the FIFO threshold bits in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register are configured for an empty FIFO (FTH[2:0] set
to 000b), an interrupt is generated if the register contains no data (FLTH[2:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xSR register are
less than 001b). (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register is set to 1 by hardware). When the FIFO is no longer
empty (FLTH[2:0] in R32_SAI_xSR is not 000b), i.e., when one or more data items are stored in the FIFO, this
interrupt (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register) is cleared by hardware.
When the FIFO threshold bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register is configured to trigger on one-quarter FIFO fill
(FTH[2:0] set to 001b), an interrupt is generated if less than one-quarter of the FIFO contains data (FLTH[2:0] bits
in R32_SAI_xSR are less than 010b). (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register is set to 1 by hardware). When
at least one-quarter of the FIFO contains data (FLTH[2:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xSR register are greater than or equal
to 010b), this interrupt (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register) is cleared by hardware.
When the FIFO threshold bits in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register are configured for half-full FIFO (FTH[2:0] set to
010b), an interrupt is generated if less than half of the FIFO contains data (FLTH[2:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xSR
register are less than 011b). (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register is set to 1 by hardware). When at least half
of the FIFO contains data (FLTH[2:0] bits in R32_SAI_xSR are greater than or equal to 011b), this interrupt (the
FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register) is cleared by hardware.
When the FIFO threshold bits in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register are configured to three-quarters full (FTH[2:0] set
to 011b), an interrupt is generated if less than three-quarters of the FIFOs contain data (FLTH[2:0] bits in the
R32_SAI_xSR register are less than 100b). (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register is set to 1 by hardware).
When at least three-quarters of the FIFO contains data (the FLTH[2:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xSR register are greater
than or equal to 100b), this interrupt (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register) is cleared by hardware.
When the FIFO threshold bits in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register are configured for a full FIFO (FTH[2:0] set to
100b), an interrupt is generated if the FIFO is not full (R32_SAI_xSR register FLTH[2:0] bits less than 101b). (the
FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register is set to 1 by hardware). When the FIFO is full (FLTH[2:0] bits in the
R32_SAI_xSR register equal 101b), this interrupt (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register) is cleared by
hardware.
Generate an interrupt in receive mode
According to the FIFO configuration in receiving mode, an interrupt is generated:

When the FIFO threshold bits in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register are configured for an empty FIFO (FTH[2:0] set
to 000b), an interrupt is generated if at least one data bit is present in the R32_SAI_xDATAR register (FLTH[2:0]
bits in the R32_SAI_xSR register are greater than or equal to 001b). (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register is
set to 1 by hardware). When the FIFO becomes empty (FLTH[2:0] in the R32_SAI_xSR register equals 000b), i.e.,
when no data is stored in the FIFO, this interrupt (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register) is cleared by hardware.
When the FIFO threshold bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register is configured for one-quarter FIFO fill (FTH[2:0]
set to 001b), an interrupt is generated if at least one-quarter of the FIFO data cells are available (R32_SAI_xSR
register FLTH[2:0] bits greater than or equal to 010b). (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register is set to 1 by
hardware). When less than one-quarter of the FIFO data cells are available (FLTH[2:0] bits in R32_SAI_xSR are
less than 010b), this interrupt (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register) is cleared by hardware.
When the FIFO threshold bits in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register are configured for half-full FIFO (FTH[2:0] set to
010b), an interrupt is generated if at least half of the FIFO data cells are available (FLTH[2:0] bits in the
R32_SAI_xSR register are greater than or equal to 011b). (The FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register is set to 1
by hardware). When less than half of the FIFO data cells are available (FLTH[2:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xSR register
are less than 011b), this interrupt (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register) is cleared by hardware.
When the FIFO threshold bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register is configured to three-quarters full (FTH[2:0] set to
011b), an interrupt is generated if at least three-quarters of the FIFO data cells are available (FLTH[2:0] bits in
SAI_xSR are greater than or equal to 100b). (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register is set to 1 by hardware).
When less than three-quarters of the FIFO data cells are available (the FLTH[2:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xSR register
are less than 100b), this interrupt (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register) is cleared by hardware.
When the FIFO threshold bits in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register are configured for FIFO full (FTH[2:0] set to 100b),
an interrupt is generated if the FIFO is full (R32_SAI_xSR register FLTH[2:0] bits equal 101b) (the FREQ bit in
the R32_SAI_xSR register is set to 1 by hardware). When the FIFO is not full (FLTH[2:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xSR
register are less than 101b), this interrupt (the FREQ bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register) is cleared by hardware.
Note: Similar to interrupt generation, if the DMAEN bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register is set to 1, the SAI can
utilize DMA.
36.3.7 AC'97 Link Controller
SAI can function as an AC'97 link controller. This mode is configured via the PRTCFG[1:0] bits in the
R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register. When this protocol is selected, numerous configuration fields are ignored.
Consequently, the number of slots and slot size are fixed, and the frame synchronization signal must be fully defined
with a fixed waveform. Failure to meet these requirements will prevent SAI from operating correctly.
The NBSLOT[3:0] bits and SLOTSZ[1:0] bits will be ignored;
- The number of slots is fixed at 13. The first slot is 16 bits wide, while all other slots are 20 bits wide (data slots);
- The FBOFF[4:0] bits in the SAI_xSLOTR register are ignored;
- The SAI_xFRCR register is ignored;
- MCLK is not used.
Regardless of whether the master or slave configuration is adopted, since the AC'97 link controller drives the FS
signal, the FS signal generated by the asynchronous module will be automatically configured as an output.

register is enabled, the flag CNRDY in the R32_SAI_xSR register will be set to 1 and an interrupt will be generated.
This flag is dedicated to AC'97 protocol.
Clock generator programming in AC'97 mode
In AC'97 mode, the frame length is fixed at 256 bits, and its frequency should be set to 48 kHz. The regulars
specified in Section 36.3.1: SAI Clock Generator should be applied with FRL=255 to generate the appropriate frame
rate (FFS).

36.3.8 SPDIF Output
SPDIF (Sony/Philips Digital Interface) is a digital audio interconnect for consumer audio equipment, designed to
transmit audio over reasonably short distances. The SPDIF interface is available only in transmit mode and supports
the IEC 60958 standard. SPDIF mode can be selected by setting the PRTCFG[1:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1
register to 01b.
For the SPDIF protocol:
1) Enable only the SD data line;
2) Release the FS, SCK, and MCLK I/O pins;
3) To enable the SAI clock generator and manage the data rate on the SD line, force the MODE[1] bit to 0 to select
master mode;
4) Force the data size to 24 bits. Values set in DS[2:0] bits of the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register are ignored;
5) The clock generator must be configured to define the symbol rate, where the known-bit clock should be twice
the symbol rate. Data is encoded using the Manchester protocol;
6) Ignore the SAI_xFRCR and SAI_xSLOTR registers. Internally configure the SAI to comply with SPDIF protocol
requirements, as shown in Figure 36-0.
Figure 36-10 SPDIF format
The SPDIF block contains 192 frames. Each frame consists of two 32-bit subframes, typically one for the left
channel and one for the right channel. Each subframe begins with a 4-bit SOPD mode bit, which specifies whether
the subframe marks the start of the block (and identifies Channel A), identifies Channel A within the block, or refers
to Channel B (see Table 36-3). The subsequent 28 bits contain channel information, comprising 24 data bits and 4
status bits.
Table 36-3 SOPD mode
Header coding
SOPD The last digit is The last digit is Description
0 1
B 11101000 00010111 Channel A data, and is the start subframe of a block.
W 11100100 00011011 Channel B data
M 11100010 00011101 Channel A data
The data transmission of SPDIF should be filled in the R32_SAI_xDATAR register according to the following:
- R32_SAI_xDATAR[26:24] contains channel status bits, user bits, and validity bits;
V1.8 775

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
- R32_SAI_xDATAR[23:0] contains the 24-bit data for the channel under consideration.
Note: (1) If the data size is 20 bits, map the data to R32_SAI_xDATAR[23:4].
(2) If the data size is 16 bits, map the data to R32_SAI_xDATAR[23:8].
Figure 36-11 R32_SAI_xDATAR register data schematic diagram
Note: R32_SAI_xDATAR[23] always stands for MSB. When performing transmission, LSB always takes precedence.
SAI first sends the appropriate header of each subframe in the block, and then sends R32_SAI_xDATAR (encoded
in Manchester protocol) on the SD line. SAI ends the subframe by transmitting parity bits calculated as described
in Table 36-4.
Table 36-4 Odd parity bits
R32_SAI_xDATAR[26:0] The value of the transmission parity bit
P

Odd number of 1 1
In SPDIF mode, underflow is the only error flag used in R32_SAI_xSR register. Since SAI can only work in the
send mode, to recover from the underflow error detected by the underflow interrupt or underflow status bit, the
following steps should be performed in sequence:
1) If DMA is already in use, disable the DMA stream via the DMA peripheral.
2) Disable SAI operation and verify physical disablement by polling the SAIEN bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1
register.
3) Clear the flag by writing a 1 to the OVRUDR bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register.
4) Flush the FIFO by setting the FFLUSH bit to 1 in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register. The software must point to
the subsequent data address corresponding to the start of the new data block (data in header B). If DMA is in use,
update the DMA source start address pointer accordingly.
5) Re-enable the DMA stream if the DMA controller resumes data transfer based on the new source start address
pointer.
6) Re-enable the SAI by setting the SAIEN bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register to 1.

36.3.9 Stereo/Mono
In transmit mode, if the number of slots equals 2 (with the NBSLOT[3:0] bits of the R32_SAI_xSLOTR register
set to 0001b), mono mode can be addressed without any data preprocessing in memory. In this case, since the data
from Slot 0 is copied to data Slot 1 during transmission, the FIFO access time is reduced by half.
To enable mono mode, the following steps are required:
1) Set the MONO bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register to 1;
2) Set the NBSLOT bit in the R32_SAI_xSLOTR register to 1 and configure the SLOTEN bit to 3.
In receive mode, the MONO bit setting to 1 is only meaningful when the Slot count equals 2 (same as in transmit
mode). When this bit is set to 1, only data from Slot 0 will be stored in the FIFO. Data from Slot 1 is discarded as
it is considered identical to the previous slot's data. If the data stream in receive mode is a true stereo audio stream
where the left and right channel data are distinctly different, the MONO bit is irrelevant. The conversion from the
output stereo file to an equivalent mono file is handled by software.
36.3.10 Mute Mode
When the audio sub-module is used as a transmitter or receiver, the mute mode can be used.
Audio sub-module in transmission mode
In transmit mode, mute mode can be selected at any time. Mute mode is effective for all audio frames. During frame
transmission, mute mode can be enabled by setting the MUTE bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register to 1. This mute
mode bit is latched only at the end of a frame. If the MUTE bit is set to 1 at the end of a frame, mute mode activates
at the start of the next audio frame and persists throughout its entire duration until the next frame ends. The bit is
then latched to determine whether the subsequent frame remains a mute frame.
If the number of slots set via the NBSLOT[3:0] bits in the R32_SAI_xSLOTR register is less than or equal to 2,
you can specify whether the value sent in mute mode is 0 or the last value for each slot. This is selected via the
MUTEVAL bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register.
If the number of slots set in the NBSLOT[3:0] bits of the R32_SAI_xSLOTR register exceeds 2, the MUTEVAL
bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register becomes meaningless since a value of 0 is sent on every bit of each slot.
In mute mode, the FIFO pointer continues to increment. This means that data requested for transmission in the FIFO
during mute mode will be discarded.
Audio sub-module in receiving mode
In receive mode, for a given number of consecutive audio frames (R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register MUTECNT[5:0]
bits), if zero is received in all declared active slots of the audio frame, a mute pattern from an external transmitter
is detected. Upon detecting the corresponding number of mute frames, the MUTEDET flag in the R32_SAI_xSR
register is set to 1 and triggers an interrupt if the MUTEDETIE bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register is set to 1.
V1.8 777

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
The mute frame counter is reset when the audio submodule is disabled or when at least one data frame is received
within a valid slot. An interrupt is generated only once when the counter reaches the value specified in the
MUTECNT[5:0] bits. Subsequent interrupt events are reinitialized when the counter is reset.
Note: Mute mode is not available for SPDIF audio module.
36.3.11 Compressed Expansion Mode
In the field of mobile communications, pre-processing of data for transmission often involves the application of
data compression and decompression algorithms.
The application can select whether to process data before transmission on the SD serial output line (compression)
and whether to decompress data after reception on the SD serial input line (expansion) based on the COMP[1:0]
bits of the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register (used only when TDM mode is selected), as shown in Figure 36-11. The two
supported compression/decompression modes are μ-Law and A-Law, both of which are standards recommended by
CCITT G.711.
The μ-Law standard, adopted in the United States and Japan, permits a 14-bit dynamic range (R32_SAI_xCFGR2
register COMP[1:0] bits set to 10b). The European A-Law standard supports a 13-bit dynamic range
(R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register COMP[1:0] bits set to 11b).
Regarding the calculation method for μ-Law or A-Law compression/expansion standards, based on the setting of
the CPL bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2 register, either 1's complement or 2's complement may be used for
computation.
In both μ-Law and A-Law standards, data is encoded in an 8-bit format aligned to the most significant bit (MSB),
and the width of data after compression/expansion processing remains consistently 8 bits.
Therefore, when the SAI audio module is enabled (R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register SAIEN bit set to 1) and either of
these two compression/expansion modes is selected via the COMP[1:0] bits, the DS[2:0] bits of the
R32_SAI_xCFGR1 register are forced to 010b. If no compression/expansion processing is required, the COMP[1:0]
bits should remain cleared.
Specifically, if the SAI audio module is configured as a transmitter and the COMP[1] bit in the R32_SAI_xCFGR2
register is set to 1, the compression mode is employed. If the SAI audio module is declared as a receiver, the
expansion algorithm is used.
Figure 36-12 Data compressed expansion hardware in audio module of SAI
V1.8 778

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
Note: Not applicable when AC'97 is selected.
Output data line management on invalid Slot
In the transmission mode, when an invalid Slot is transmitted on the data line, the behavior of SD line output can
be controlled by TRIS bit.
- When an invalid slot is transmitted, the SAI forces the SD output line to 0.
- After the last data bit is transmitted, the SD output line is placed in a high-impedance state to release the data
line for use by other transmitters connected to this node.
2 transmitters must not simultaneously drive the same SD output pin to prevent short-circuit conditions. To ensure
a gap exists during transmission, if the data is less than 32 bits, set the SLOTSZ[1:0] bits in the
R32_SAI_xSLOTR register to 10b to expand the data to 32 bits. Subsequently, if the next slot is declared invalid,
the SD output pin will be tri-stated at the end of the LSD of the valid slot (during the zero-padding phase to extend
data to 32 bits).
Additionally, if the product of the number of slots and the slot size is less than the frame length, the SD output line
will be tri-stated when supplementing the audio frame end with zero-padding.
Figure 36-13 illustrates these behaviors.

36.3.12 Error Flag
SAI uses the following error flags:
- FIFO overflow/underflow;
- Frame sync advance detection;
- Frame sync delay detection;
- Codec not ready (AC'97 only);
- Master mode clock configuration error.

36.3.12.1 FIFO Overflow/Underflow (OVRUDR)
The FIFO overflow/underflow bit is the OVRUDR bit in R32_SAI_xSR register.
Since audio modules can be used as both receivers and transmitters, and each audio module in the specified SAI
has its own R32_SAI_xSR register, overflow or underflow errors share the same bit.

Overflow
If the audio module is configured as a receiver, an overflow occurs when audio frame data is received while the
FIFO is full and cannot store any more received data. In this case, the received data is lost, and the OVRUDR flag
in the R32_SAI_xSR register is set to 1. If the OVRUDRIE bit in the R32_SAI_xINTENR register is set to 1, an
V1.8                                              781

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
interrupt is also generated. The internal system records the slot number at the time of overflow. The FIFO cannot
store additional data until space is freed to accommodate new data. Once the FIFO has freed space for at least one
data item, the SAI audio module receiver begins receiving new data from the new audio frame starting from the slot
number internally recorded after the overflow detection. This prevents data slot misalignment in the target memory.
Refer to Figure 36-15 for details.
To clear the OVRUDR flag, set the OVRUDR bit in the R32_SAI_xSR register to 1.

Underflow
When the audio module in SAI is used as a transmitter, if the FIFO is empty when data needs to be sent, underflow
may occur. If underflow is detected, the Slot number of the event will be stored and the MUTE value (00b) will be
sent until the FIFO is ready to send the data corresponding to the Slot where underflow is detected. See Figure 36-
16 for details. This can avoid synchronization failure between memory pointer and Slot in audio frame.
The underflow event will set the OVRUDR flag in the R32_SAI_xSR register to 1, and if the OVRUDRIE bit in
the R32_SAI_ xINTENR register is set to 1, an interrupt will be generated. To clear this flag, just write 1 to bit
OVRUDR in R32_SAI_xSR register.
When the audio submodule is configured as master mode or slave mode, an underflow event will occur.
