40.5.5 Synchronous Transaction
The memory clock FMC_CLK is a divisor of HCLK. It depends on the value of CLKDIV and the MWID/HB data
size, as shown in the following formula:
FMC_CLK Frequency division ratio = max (CLKDIV+1, MWID (HB data size))
When MWID is 16-bit or 8-bit, the frequency division ratio of FMC_CLK is always defined by the setting value of
CLKDIV.
When MWID is 32-bit, the frequency division ratio of FMC_CLK also depends on the size of HB data.
Example:
 LKDIV=1, MWID=32 bits, when HB data size=8 bits, FMC_CLK=HCLK/4.
 CLKDIV=1, MWID=16 bits, when HB data size =8 bits, FMC_CLK=HCLK/2.
NOR Flash specifies the minimum time from NADV enable to CLK high. In order to meet this limitation, FMC
will not send the clock to the memory within the first internal clock cycle of synchronous access (before NADV is
enabled). This ensures that the rising edge of the memory clock appears in the middle of the NADV low pulse.
Data delay and NOR delay
Data delay is the number of cycles to wait before sampling data. The value of DATLAT must match the delay value
specified in the NORFLASH configuration register. When NADV is low in the data delay count, FMC will not
count the clock period.
Some NOR Flash count the NADV low period in the data delay count, so the exact relationship between the NOR
Flash delay and the FMC DATLAT parameter can be any of the following:
 NOR Flash delay =(DATLAT+2) CLK clock cycles.
 NOR Flash delay =(DATLAT+3) CLK clock cycles.
Recently, some memories will enable NWAIT in the delay phase. In this case, you can set DATLAT to the minimum
value. Then, FMC will sample the data and wait long enough to evaluate whether the data is valid. In this way, FMC
can detect the delay time in the memory, so as to process the real data.
Other memories will not enable NWAIT during the delay. In this case, the delay of FMC and memory must be set
correctly, otherwise invalid data may be misused as valid data, or valid data may be lost in the initial stage of
V1.8 871

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
memory access.
Single burst transmission
When the selected storage area is configured in synchronous burst mode, for example, if an HB single burst
transaction is requested from a 16-bit memory, FMC will execute a burst transaction with a length of 1 (if the HB
transmission is 16 bits) or a burst transaction with a length of 2 (if the HB transmission is 32 bits), and then disable
the chip selection signal at the last data strobe.
Compared with asynchronous read operation, this is not the most efficient transmission method in terms of cycle.
However, random asynchronous reading requires reprogramming the memory access mode first, so the total time
will be longer.
Cross the border page of Cellular RAM1.5
Cellular RAM1.5 does not allow burst access to cross page boundaries. When the CPSIZE bit in the
R32_FMC_BCR1 register is configured according to the memory page size to reach the memory page size, the
FMC controller will automatically separate the burst access.
Waiting management
For synchronous NOR Flash, NWAIT will be evaluated after the configured delay period (equivalent to (DATLAT+2)
CLK clock cycles).
If NWAIT is valid (low level when WAITPOL=0 and high level when WAITPOL=1), the waiting state will be
inserted until NWAIT is invalid (high level when WAITPOL=0 and low level when WAITPOL=1).
When NWAIT is invalid, the data will be considered valid immediately (bit WAITCFG=1) or at the next clock edge
(bit WAITCFG=0).
During the waiting period when the NWAIT signal is inserted, the controller will continue to send clock pulses to
the memory to keep the chip select and output enable signals valid. But the data is not considered valid.
In burst mode, NOR Flash NWAIT signal has two timing configurations:
 Flash sends out NWAIT signal (the default value after reset) one data period before the waiting period.
 Flash sends out NWAIT signal during the waiting period.
FMC supports these 2 configurations of NOR Flash waiting period, and each chip selection is configured through
the WAITCFG bit (x=0..3) pin of R32_FMC_BCRx register.

Note: PSRAM (CRAM) exhibits unpredictable data latency durations due to internal refresh cycles. Consequently,
these memories emit NWAIT signals throughout the delay phase to extend latency as required. For PSRAM (CRAM),
the DATLAT field must be set to 0. This instructs the FMC to immediately exit the delay phase, commence sampling
NWAIT from the memory, and initiate read or write operations once the memory is ready.
This method also applies to the latest generation of synchronous Flash. Unlike earlier Flash types, these Flash
devices generate an NWAIT signal (refer to the specific Flash datasheet for details).

40.6.4 NAND Flash Operation
The Command Latch Enable (CLE) signal and Address Latch Enable (ALE) signal for NAND Flash devices are
driven by the address signals from the FMC controller. This means that to send a command or address to the NAND
Flash, the CPU must perform a write operation to a specific address within its memory space.
A typical page read operation from a NAND Flash device requires the following steps:
1) Based on NAND Flash characteristics (PWID bit indicates NAND Flash data bus width, PTYP=1, set
PWAITEN=0 or 1 as required; For timing configuration, refer to Section 40.4.2: NAND Flash Address
Mapping), configure the FMC_PCR and FMC_PMEM registers (for certain devices, configure the
R32_FMC_PATT register; refer to Section 40.6.5: NAND Flash Pre-Wait Function). This process configures
and enables the corresponding storage regions.
2) The CPU performs a byte write operation to the general memory space, where the data byte equals one Flash
command byte (e.g., 0x00 for Samsung NAND Flash devices). During the write enable period (a low-level
pulse on NWE), the LE input of the NAND Flash is active. Consequently, the written byte is interpreted as a
command for the NAND Flash. Once this command is latched by the memory device, it need not be rewritten
during subsequent page read operations.
3) By writing the four bytes STARTAD[7:0], STARTAD[16:9], STARTAD[24:17], and STARTAD[25] (for
64Mb*8-bit NAND Flash) into the general memory space or feature space (three bytes for smaller capacity
devices), the CPU can send the start address (STARTAD) for the read operation. During the write enable period
V1.8 890

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
(a low-level pulse on NWE), the ALE input of the NAND Flash device is active, causing the written byte to be
treated as the starting address for the read operation. Utilizing the feature memory space, an alternative timing
configuration of the FMC can be employed to implement the pre-wait functionality required by certain NAND
Flash devices (for details, refer to Section 40.6.5: NAND Flash Pre-Wait Functionality).
4) The controller waits for the NAND Flash to become ready (R/NB signal high) before initiating a new access to
the same or another storage area. During this wait period, the controller maintains the NCE signal active (low).
5) The CPU can then execute byte-read operations from general memory space, thereby reading NAND Flash
pages (data field + spare field) byte by byte.
6) The next NAND Flash page can be read without any CPU command or address write operation. This can be
achieved in three distinct ways:
- Perform the operation described in Step 5
- Randomly access a new address by restarting the operation in Step 3
- Send a new command to the NAND Flash device by restarting Step 2

40.6.6 Error Correction Code (ECC) Calculation (NAND Flash)
The FMC NAND card controller incorporates two error correction code (ECC) calculation hardware modules, one
for each storage area. These modules reduce the host CPU workload during software-based ECC processing.
Both ECC modules are identical and associated with storage areas 2 and 3, respectively. Consequently, hardware
ECC calculations do not apply to memory connected to storage area 4.
During read or write operations to NAND Flash, the ECC algorithm employed in the FMC corrects single-bit errors
and detects double-bit errors for every 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, or 8192 bytes. This operation is based on the
Hamming code algorithm and includes the calculation of row and column parity.
Whenever the NAND Flash storage area is active, the ECC module monitors the NAND Flash data bus and
read/write signals (NCE and NWE).
ECC operates as follows:
 When accessing NAND Flash memory regions 2 or 3, it latches data appearing on the D[15:0] bus and uses it
for ECC computation.
 When accessing any other address in the NAND Flash, the ECC logic enters idle state and performs no
operation. Therefore, write operations defining NAND Flash commands or addresses are invalid during ECC
computation.
After the host CPU completes the read/write operation for the required number of bytes to the NAND Flash, it must
read the R32_FMC_ECCR register to retrieve the computed value. Following this read operation, these registers
should be cleared by resetting the ECCEN bit to zero. To compute a new data block, the ECCEN bit in the
FMC_PCR register must be set to 1.
To perform ECC calculation:
1) Enable the ECCEN bit in the R32_FMC_PCR register.
2) Write data to the NAND Flash page. During NAND page write, the ECC module calculates the ECC value.
3) Read the ECC value provided in the R32_FMC_ECCR register and store it in a variable.
4) Clear and then enable the ECCEN bit in the R32_FMC_PCR register. Read back the written data from the NAND
page. During the NAND page read operation, the ECC module will compute the ECC value.
5) Read the new ECC value provided in the R32_FMC_ECCR register.
6) If the two read ECC values match, no correction is needed. Otherwise, an ECC error exists, and the software
correction routine will return information indicating whether the error can be corrected.

40.7 SDRAM Controller
40.7.1 Main Features of SDRAM Controller
The main features of SDRAM controller are as follows:
  Support word, half-word, and byte access
  Power-down mode
  CAS delays 1, 2, 3
  Self-refresh mode
  Programmable timing parameters
  Software-configurable SDRAM power-up initialization
  2 independently configurable SDRAM storage regions
  Multi-region ping-pong access
  SDRAM clock can be HCLK, HCLK/2, or HCLK/3
  Supports automatic refresh operation with programmable refresh rate
  8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit memory data bus width
  Automatic storage region boundary management
  Read FIFO cache with 6 lines × 32-bit depth (6 × 14-bit address tags)
  13-bit address row, 11-bit address column, 4 internal storage regions: 4*16M*32bit (256MB), 4*16M*16bit
(128MB), 4*16M*8bit (64MB)

40.7.2 SDRAM External Memory Interface Signal
At startup, the SDRAMI/O pin used to connect the FMCSDRAM controller with the external SDRAM device must
be configured through the user application. Unused SDRAM controller I/O pins of application programs can be
used for other purposes.

40.7.3 SDRAM Controller Function Description
All SDRAM controller outputs (signal, address and data) can be configured to change on the falling edge of the
memory clock (FMC_SDCLK).
SDRAM initialization
The initialization sequence is managed by software. If 2 memory regions are used, the target memory region bits
CTB1 and CTB2 in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register must be set to 1, and the initialization sequences for memory
region 1 and memory region 2 must be generated at the same time:
1) Program the memory device characteristics into the R32_FMC_SDCRx registers. The SDRAM clock frequency,
RBURST, and RPIPE characteristics must be programmed into the R32_FMC_SDCR1 register.
2) Program the memory device timing into the R32_FMC_SDTRx registers. TRP and TRC timing must be
programmed into the R32_FMC_SDTR1 register.
3) Set MODE[2:0] in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register to “001” and configure the target memory region bits (CTB1
and/or CTB2) in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register to begin clocking the memory (SDCKE driven high).
4) Wait for the specified delay cycle. Typical delay is 100μs.
5) Set MODE[2:0] in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register to “010” and configure the target memory area bits (CTB1
and/or CTB2) in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register to send the “Full Precharge” command.
6) Set MODE[2:0] in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register to “011” and configure the target storage area (CTB1 and/or
CTB2) and the number of Non-Repeatable Automatic Refresh (NRFS) commands in the R32_FMC_SDCMR
register.
7) Configure the MRD field according to the SDRAM device. Set MODE[2:0] in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register
to “100” and configure the target storage area bits (CTB1 and/or CTB2) in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register to send
the “Load Mode Register” command and program the SDRAM device. Specifically:
a) The CAS delay must be selected based on the value in R32_FMC_SDCR1/2;
b) The burst length (BL) must be set to 1 by configuring the MRD[2:0] bits in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register to
000.
If the mode registers for the two SDRAM storage regions differ, this step must be repeated twice—once for each
storage region—with the corresponding target storage region bit set to 1.
8) Program the refresh rate in the R32_FMC_SDRTR register. The refresh rate corresponds to the delay between
refresh cycles. Its value must be compatible with the SDRAM device.
At this stage, the SDRAM device is ready to receive commands. If a system reset occurs during an SDRAM access,
V1.8 898

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
the data bus may still be driven by the SDRAM device. Therefore, the SDRAM device must be reinitialized after
reset before the NOR Flash/PSRAM/SRAM or NAND Flash controller can issue new access commands.
Note: If two SDRAM devices are connected to the FMC, simultaneous access to both devices via the command mode
register (loading the mode register command) will issue access commands based on the timing parameters (TMRD
and TRAS timing) configured for SDRAM memory region 1 in the R32_FMC_SDTR1 register.
SDRAM controller write cycle
SDRAM controller can receive single and burst write requests and treat them as a single memory access. In both
cases, the SDRAM controller will track the valid lines of each storage area, so as to be able to make continuous
write access to different storage areas (multi-storage area ping-pong access). Before performing any write access,
the WP bit in R32_FMC_SDCRx register must be cleared to prohibit write protection of SDRAM storage area.
The SDRAM controller always checks for the next access:
1) If the next access occurs on the same row or another valid row, the write operation proceeds directly.
2) If the next access points to an invalid row, the SDRAM controller generates a precharge command, activates the
new row, and initializes the write command.

SDRAM controller read cycle
SDRAM controller can receive single and burst read requests and treat them as a single memory access. In both
cases, the SDRAM controller will track the valid lines of each storage area, so as to be able to perform continuous
read access to different storage areas (multi-storage area ping-pong access).

The FMC SDRAM controller features a cacheable read FIFO (6 lines × 32 bits) that pre-fetches read data during
CAS latency cycles and RPIPE delays according to the following formula. The RBURST bit in the
R32_FMC_SDCR1 register must be set to 1 to accept the next read access. Expected data count = CAS latency +
1 + (RPIPE latency) / 2, example:
 CAS latency = 3, RPIPE latency = 0: Four data items (uncommitted) stored in the FIFO.
 CAS latency = 3, RPIPE latency = 2: Five data items (uncommitted) stored in the FIFO.
Each row in the read FIFO has a 14-bit address tag to identify its contents: 11 bits for the column address, 2 bits for
selecting the internal memory region and valid row, and 1 bit for selecting the SDRAM device. During HB burst
reads, if the end of the row is reached prematurely, the data read ahead (not yet committed) is not stored in the read
FIFO. For single read accesses, the data is correctly stored in the read FIFO.
Whenever a read request occurs, the SDRAM controller checks:
 Whether the address matches one of the address tags. If a match is found, data is read directly from the FIFO,
the corresponding address tag/row content is cleared, and the remaining data in the FIFO is compressed to
avoid empty rows.
 Otherwise, a new read command is sent to memory and the FIFO is updated with the new data. If the FIFO is
full, earlier data will be lost.

During a read access or precharge command, the read FIFO will refresh and prepare to fill with new data.
Upon receiving the first read request, if the current access has not yet reached a row boundary, the SDRAM
controller will accept the next read access during the CAS latency cycle and RPIPE latency (if configured). This is
achieved by incrementing the memory address. The following conditions must be met:
 The RBURST control bit in the R32_FMC_SDCR1 register must be set to 1
Address management depends on the next HB request:
 The next HB request is consecutive (HB burst)
In this case, the SDRAM controller will increment the address.
 The next HB request is not consecutive
- If the new read request targets the same row as the previous request or another valid row, the new address
is transmitted to the memory while the master device halts operations during the CAS latency period,
awaiting new data from the memory.
- If the new read request targets an invalid row, the SDRAM controller generates a precharge command,
activates the new row, and initializes the read command.
If RURST is set to 0, the read FIFO is not used.
Row and storage area boundary management
V1.8 901

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
When a read/write access crosses a row boundary, if the next read/write access is continuous and the current access
has been executed to the row boundary, the SDRAM controller will perform the following operations:
1) Precharge the active row;
2) Activate the new row;
3) Initiate the read/write command.
For all column and data bus width configurations, automatic row activation at row boundaries is supported.
The SDRAM controller may insert additional clock cycles between the following commands as required:
 Inserted between the precharge and activate commands to match the TRP parameter (only when the next access
targets another row within the same memory area).
 Inserted between the activate and read commands to match the TRCD parameter.
These parameters are defined in the FMC_SDTRx register.
For information on row boundary crossing reads and burst write accesses, refer to the diagram below.

Precharge Activate Row Write Command
If the next access is continuous and the current access crosses the storage area boundary, the SDRAM controller
will activate the first row of the next storage area and issue a new read/write command. There are two possible
situations:
 If the current memory area is not the last memory area, the active row in the new memory area must be
precharged. For various row/column and data bus width configurations, the automatic activation of the next
row at the boundary of the storage area is supported.
 If the current storage area is the last storage area, the automatic activation of the next row is only supported
when addressing SDRAM devices with 13-bit rows, 11-bit columns, 4 internal storage areas and 32-bit data
bus. Otherwise, SDRAM address range will be violated and HB error will be generated.
 For the SDRAM memory with 13-bit row address, 11-column address, 4 internal storage areas and 32-bit bus
width, the SDRAM controller will continue the read/write operation through the second SDRAM device
(assuming that the second SDRAM device is initialized):
- The SDRAM controller will activate the first row (assuming that there is a valid row in the first internal
storage area after precharging the valid row) and issue a new read/write command;
- If the first row is activated, the SDRAM controller will only issue read/write commands.
SDRAM controller refresh cycle
The automatic refresh command is used to refresh the contents of SDRAM devices. SDRAM controller will send
automatic refresh command periodically. It uses an internal COUNTer to load the count value in the
R32_FMC_SDRTR register. This value defines the number of memory clock cycles (refresh rate) between refresh
cycles. When the value of the counter reaches zero, an internal pulse will be generated.
If there is an ongoing memory access, the automatic refresh request will be delayed. However, when memory access
and automatic refresh request occur at the same time, the automatic refresh request is given priority.
If the memory is accessed during the automatic refresh, the access request is cached and processed after the
automatic refresh is completed.
If a new automatic refresh request appears when the last automatic refresh request has not been completed, the RE
(refresh error) bit in the status register will be set to 1. If this bit is enabled (REIE=1), an interrupt will be generated.
V1.8 903

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
If the SDRAM rows are not idle (not all rows are closed), the SDRAM controller will generate a PALL (pre-charge
all) command before automatic refresh.
If the automatic refresh command is generated by the R32_FMC_SDCMR command mode register (mode bit =
"011"), the PALL command (mode bit = "010") must be issued first.
40.7.4 Low-power Mode
2 low-power modes are available:
 Self-Refresh Mode
The SDRAM device performs automatic refresh cycles to retain data without requiring an external clock.
 Power-Down Mode
The SDRAM controller performs automatic refresh cycles.
Self-refresh mode
This mode is selected by setting the MODE position to '101' and configuring the target storage area bits (CTB1
and/or CTB2) in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register.
The SDRAM clock ceases operation after the TRAS delay, while the internal refresh timer only stops counting when
one of the following conditions is met:
 A self-refresh command was issued to both devices.
 One of the devices was not activated (the SDRAM storage area was not initialized).
Before entering self-refresh mode, the SDRAM controller automatically issues a PALL command.
If the write data FIFO is not empty, all data will be sent to memory before self-refresh mode activates, and the
BUSY status flag remains set to 1.
In self-refresh mode, all inputs to the SDRAM device are invalid except for SDCKE, which must remain low.
SDRAM devices must remain in self-refresh mode for a minimum duration equal to the TRAS time and must be
capable of sustaining self-refresh mode for extended periods. To ensure this minimum duration, the BUSY status
flag remains high throughout the TRAS delay period following self-refresh activation.
The SDRAM controller immediately generates a command sequence to exit self-refresh mode upon selection of an
SDRAM device. After memory access completes, the selected device remains in normal mode.
To exit self-refresh mode, the MODE bit must be set to “000” (normal mode) and the target storage area bits (CTB1
and/or CTB2) within the R32_FMC_SDCMR register must be configured.

If the write data FIFO is not empty, all data will be sent to memory before power-down mode is activated.
The SDRAM controller will exit power-down mode immediately after an SDRAM device is selected. After memory
access completes, the selected SDRAM device will remain in normal mode.
During power-down mode, all input/output buffers of the SDRAM device will be disabled, except for SDCKE,
which remains low.
SDRAM devices can't stay in power-down mode for longer than refresh cycle, and they can't perform self-refresh
cycle. Therefore, the SDRAM controller performs refresh by:
V1.8 905

CH32H417 Reference Manual                                          https://wch-ic.com
1) Exit power-down mode and drive SDCKE high.
2) Generate the PALL command. (provided an activation line exists in power-down mode)
3) Generate an auto-refresh command
4) Drive SDCKE low again to return to power-down mode.
To exit power-down mode, the MODE bit must be set to “000” (normal mode) and the target storage area bits (CTB1
and/or CTB2) must be configured in the R32_FMC_SDCMR register.

Chapter 41 Encryption Module (ECDC)
The system has built-in block cipher algorithm module, which supports AES and SM4 block cipher algorithms and
electronic codebook (ECB) and counter (CTR) modes. The module completes one encryption and decryption
process with 128-bit data size as the basic unit, and provides a DMA encryption and decryption mode for data in
memory and a single encryption and decryption mode for SFR registers.
41.1 Main Features
 ECB and CTR modes for SM4 algorithm with 128-bit keys
 ECB and CTR modes for AES algorithm with 128/192/256-bit keys
 Support direct encryption of individual 128-bit data via software writing to SFRs
 Support DMA-based (memory-to-memory) encryption/decryption of software-specified data blocks
41.2 AES/SM4 Algorithm
The Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithm is a block cipher that employs a symmetric block cipher
system, ranking among the most widely used symmetric-key encryption algorithms. The SM4 block cipher
algorithm is typically a dedicated block cipher designed for wireless local area networks (WLANs) and trusted
computing environments, though it can also be utilized for data encryption protection in other contexts.
During data encryption and decryption, keys must be loaded. For the AES algorithm, depending on the key length
set to 128/192/256 bits, the user key must be expanded into an expansion key of 11×128/13×128/15×128 bits,
respectively. In contrast, the SM4 algorithm expands a 128-bit user key into a 32×32-bit expanded key. These
expanded keys are stored in internal registers for convenient access during encryption and decryption operations.
41.3 ECB and CTR Mode
AES/SM4 supports two modes, electronic codebook (ECB) mode and counter (CTR) mode, in which the security
performance of CTR mode is higher than that of ECB mode. As shown in figure 41-1 and 41-2 working block
diagram.
Figure 41-1 ECB mode encryption and decryption process
Plain Text Plain Text Plain Text Plain Text
0 1 0 1
Encryption Encryption Decryption Decryption
Cipher Text Cipher Text Cipher Text Cipher Text
0 1 0 1
Encryption in ECB mode Decryption under ECB mode

Figure 41-2 CTR mode encryption and decryption process
|        | Count                  |        | Count+1      |         | Count                     |         | Count+1     |
| ------ | ---------------------- | ------ | ------------ | ------- | ------------------------- | ------- | ----------- |
|        | Encryption             |        | Encryption   |         | Encryption                |         | Encryption  |
| Plain  |                        | Plain  |              | Cipher  |                           | Cipher  |             |
|        | XOR                    |        | XOR          |         | XOR                       |         | XOR         |
| Text 0 |                        | Text 1 |              | Text 0  |                           | Text 1  |             |
|        | Cipher Text            |        | Cipher Text  |         | Plain Text                |         | Plain Text  |
|        | 0                      |        | 1            |         | 0                         |         | 1           |
|        | Encryption in CTR mode |        |              |         | Decryption under CTR mode |         |             |

In ECB mode, plaintext and ciphertext are directly mapped one-to-one; the plaintext is encrypted verbatim to
produce the ciphertext. In CTR mode, however, a 128-bit counter must be preloaded. This counter is encrypted, and
the encrypted counter is then XORed with the plaintext to generate the ciphertext. It is important to note that in CTR
decryption mode, only the counter is encrypted—it is not decrypted.

41.4 Module Application
41.4.1 Initialization of Encryption and Decryption Module
  Clock configuration: set RB_ECDC_CLKDIV_MASK bit in R32_ECEC_CTRL register to configure the
clock for module operation. If you don't use this module, you can set it to 0 and turn it off to reduce power
consumption.
  Data size end: set RB_ECDC_DAT_MOD bit of R32_ECEC_CTRL register, and you can choose the storage
mode of the size end of the encrypted and decrypted data. According to the size of a packet of 128bits(16
bytes).
  Key Expansion: During encryption and decryption, an expansion key is used instead of the user key. After
setting the user key length and content, the hardware must be instructed to perform key expansion. Once
expanded, the key is stored in the module's internal registers. Only then can normal data encryption and
decryption  proceed.  Configure  the  R32_ECEC_CTRL  register:  set  RB_ECDC_WRSRAM_EN,
RB_ECDC_ALGRM_MOD, RB_ECDC_CIPHER_MOD, and RB_ECDC_KLEN_MASK to enable SRAM
data encryption/decryption, select the encryption/decryption algorithm, specify the block cipher mode, and
define the key length. Then configure the user key register group R32_ECDC_KEY by populating it with the
user key content. After setting RB_ECDC_KEYEX_EN in the R32_ECEC_CTRL register to 1 and then
clearing it to 0, the hardware initiates the key expansion function.
  Initial counter value: When using CTR mode for encryption/decryption, an initial counter value is required.
Set the 128-bit counter value in the CTR mode counter register group R32_ECDC_IV. Each successful
completion of a data encryption/decryption cycle (128-bit data) increments the internal counter value by 1.
This counter value is not needed in ECB mode.

Memory-to-memory data conversion begins when non-zero data is written to the R32_ECDC_SRAM_LEN length
register. By checking the RB_ECDC_IF_WRSRAM bit in the R32_ECDC_INT_FG register, a value of 1 indicates
the memory-to-memory data conversion is complete, clearing the RB_ECDC_IF_WRSRAM bit status. If the
RB_ECDC_IE_WRSRAM function in the R32_ECDC_CTRL register is enabled, an interrupt service is triggered
simultaneously with setting the RB_ECDC_IF_WRSRAM flag.
Single-pass  encryption/decryption  must  be  configured  in  big-endian  mode  (RB_ECDC_DAT_MOD=1)  for
execution. The single-pass encryption/decryption conversion of 128-bit data begins with a write operation to the
upper  32  bits  of  the  R32_ECDC_SGSD  register.  By  checking  the  RB_ECDC_IF_SINGLE  bit  in  the
R32_ECDC_INT_FG register, a value of 1 indicates completion of the single 128-bit data conversion, clearing the
RB_ECDC_IF_SINGLE bit status. If the RB_ECDC_IE_SINGLE function in the R32_ECDC_CTRL register is
enabled, an interrupt service is triggered simultaneously with the setting of the RB_ECDC_IF_SINGLE flag.

Chapter 42 Digital Filter for ΣΔ Modulator (DFSDM)
DFSDM is a high-performance module dedicated to connecting external ΣΔ modulator to MCU. It contains two
external digital serial interfaces and 2 digital filters, and has flexible ΣΔ digital processing options, which can
provide the final resolution of ADC up to 24 bits. DFSDM can also select parallel data stream input from internal
ADC peripherals or device memory.
42.1 Main Features
 Provide 2 multiplexed digital serial input channels
 2 internal digital parallel channels supporting optional inputs
 Support adjustable digital signal processing
 Support up to 24-bit output data resolution
 Support signed data formats
 Support automatic data offset correction (offset value stored by user in register)
 Include 2 conversion modes: single conversion mode and continuous conversion mode
 Conversion initiation supported via software trigger, internal timer, external event, or synchronization with the
first DFSDM filter
 Supports analog watchdog
 Built-in short-circuit detector to identify saturated analog input values (lower and upper limits)
 Support open-circuit generation upon analog watchdog events and short-circuit monitoring events
 Built-in extreme value detector
 Support interrupts and DMA

42.3 Function Description
42.3.1 DFSDM Reset and Clock
DFSDM Switch Control
Global  enablement  of  the  DFSDM  interface  is  achieved  by  setting  the  DFSDMEN  bit  in  the
R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register to 1. Once the DFSDM interface is globally enabled, all configured input
channels y (y=0/1) and digital filters DFSDM_FLTx (x=0/1) will begin operation when their respective enable bits
(channel  enable  bit  CHEN  in  R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1  and  DFSDM_FLTx  enable  bit  DFEN  in
R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1) are set to 1.
The digital filter DFSDM_FLTx (x=0/1) is enabled by setting DFEN in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register to 1.
After enabling DFSDM_FLTx (DFEN=1), the Sincx digital filter unit and integrator unit will be reinitialized.
Clearing DFEN immediately halts all ongoing conversions and places DFSDM_FLTx into stop mode. All register

settings remain unchanged except for R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWSR and R32_DFSDM_FLTxISR, which are reset.
Enable channel y (y=0/1) by setting CHEN in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register to 1. Once a channel is
enabled, serial data is received from an external ΣΔ modulator or a parallel internal data source (CPU/DMA write
operations to ADCs or memory).
Before stopping the system clock and entering stop mode, the DFSDM must be globally disabled (by setting
DFSDMEN=0 in the R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register).
DFSDM Clock
The internal DFSDM clock f drives channel transceivers, digital processing modules (including digital
DFSDMCLK
filters and integrators), and subsequent auxiliary modules (such as analog watchdogs, short-circuit detectors,
extreme-value detectors, and control modules). This clock is generated by the RCC module, sourced from either the
peripheral clock HCLK or the audio clock. The DFSDM clock automatically stops in stop mode (when all
DFSDM_FLTx, x=0/1, and DFEN=0).
The DFSDM serial channel transceiver can accept an external serial clock to sample external serial data streams. If
standard SPI encoding is used, the internal DFSDM clock must be at least four times faster than the external serial
clock.
The DFSDM supports providing an external output clock signal to drive the clock input of an external ΣΔ modulator.
This output clock signal is delivered via the CKOUT pin. The frequency of the output clock signal must fall within
the range specified in the device manual and can be derived from either the DFSDM clock or the audio clock (refer
to the CKOUTSRC bit in the R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register) through a divider. The programmable range of
the divider is 2 to 256 (CKOUTDIV bit in the R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register). The audio clock is obtained by
selecting PLL_CLK via the SYSPLL_SEL[2:0] field in the RCC configuration, which in turn configures PLLCLK.
42.3.2 Serial Channel Transceiver
This peripheral features 2 multiplexed serial data channels that can be selected for conversion via individual filters,
analog watchdogs, or short-circuit detectors. These serial transceivers receive data streams from external ΣΔ
modulators. Data streams can be transmitted in SPI format (refer to the SITP bit in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1
register).
The channel is enabled by setting the CHEN bit in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register to 1.
Channel Input Selection
Serial inputs (data and clock signals) for the DATINy and CKINy pins can be redirected from subsequent channel
pins. The redirection functionality for serial input channels is configured via the CHINSEL bit in the
R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register.
Channel redirection can be used to acquire audio data from PDM (Pulse Density Modulation) stereo microphones.
A PDM stereo microphone contains one data signal and one clock signal, where the data signal provides information
for the left and right audio channels (sampling occurs on the rising edge of the clock for the left channel and on the
falling edge for the right channel).
Configuration of PDM microphone input serial channel;
 PDM microphone signals (data, clock) will be connected to the DFSDM input serial channel y (DATINy,
CKOUT) pins

 Configure channel (y-1) (mod 2) as follows:
CHINSEL=1 (input from subsequent channel ((y-1)+1) pins: DATINy and CKINy)
 Channel y: SITP=0 (data gated on rising edge) – left audio channel for channel y

Clock Signal Output
A clock signal can be provided at the CKOUT pin to drive the clock input of an external ΣΔ modulator. The CKOUT
signal frequency is derived from either the DFSDM clock or the audio clock (refer to the CKOUTSRC bit in the
R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register) via a prescaler (refer to the CKOUTDIV bit in the R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1
register). If the output clock is stopped, the CKOUT signal is placed in a low state (the output clock can be stopped
by setting CKOUTDIV=0 in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register or by setting DFSDMEN=0 in the
R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register). The output clock stop is executed at the following times:
 When CKOUTSRC=0, 4 system clock cycles after DFSDMEN cleared
 When CKOUTSRC=1, one system clock cycle and three audio clock cycles after DFSDMEN is cleared.
 Before changing CKOUTSRC, the software must wait for CKOUT to stop to avoid glitch signals on the
CKOUT pin. The output clock signal frequency must be within the range of 0 to 20MHz.
Before changing CKOUTSRC, the software must wait for CKOUT to stop, so as to avoid generating glitch signal
on CKOUT pin. The frequency of the output clock signal must be in the range of 0 ~ 20MHz.
SPI Data Input Format Operation
In SPI format, data streams are transmitted in serial format through data and clock signals. The data signal is always
provided by the datum pin. The clock signal can be provided from the outside through CKINy pin or from the inside
through the signal from CKOUT signal source.
If an external clock source is selected (SPICKSEL[1:0]=0), the data signal is sampled (DATINy pin) on the rising
or falling edge of the clock according to the SITP bit setting in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register.
Internal clock source—refer to SPICKSEL[1:0] in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register:
 CKOUT signal:
- For connecting an external ΣΔ modulator, which directly uses its clock input (from CKOUT) to generate the
output serial communication clock.
- Sampling point: Rising edge/falling edge, depending on SITP settings.

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
 CKOUT/2 signal (generated on the rising edge of CKOUT):
- Used to connect an external ΣΔ modulator, which divides the clock input (from CKOUT) by 2 to generate the
output serial communication clock. This output clock is active on each rising edge of the clock input.
- Sampling point: Every second falling edge of CKOUT.
 CKOUT/2 signal (generated on the falling edge of CKOUT):
- Used to connect an external ΣΔ modulator, which divides the clock input (from CKOUT) by 2 to generate the
output serial communication clock. This output clock change is valid on each falling edge of the clock input.
- Sampling point: Every second rising edge of CKOUT.
Note: The internal clock source can only be used when an external ΣΔ modulator employs the CKOUT signal as its
clock input (to achieve synchronous clock and data operation). Using the internal clock source eliminates the need
for a CKINy pin connection (the CKINy pin can be repurposed for other functions). When using SPI encoding, the
clock source signal frequency must fall within the range of 0 to 20 MHz and be less than f /4.

Clock Loss Detection
This feature detects the presence or absence of clock signals on channel serial clock inputs, ensuring proper
operation of conversion processes and error reporting. Clock absence detection is enabled or disabled for each input
channel y via the CKABEN bit in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register. If clock absence detection is enabled for
a given channel, it is continuously monitored. If an input clock error occurs, the clock loss flag is set to 1
(CKABF[y]=1) and an interrupt is triggered (when CKABIE=1). After the clock miss flag is cleared (via
CLRCKABF in the R32_DFSDM_FLT0ICR register), the clock miss status bit CKABF[y] is reset. When the
corresponding channel y is disabled, CKABF[y] is additionally set to 1 by hardware (if CHEN[y]=0, CKABF[y]
remains set).

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
Upon occurrence of a clock-out event, the data conversion (and/or analog watchdog and short-circuit detector) will
provide erroneous data. When clock-out is reported, the user should handle this event and discard the associated
data.
The clock-out function is only available when the system clock is used for the CKOUT signal (CKOUTSRC=0 in
the R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register).
When the transceiver is out of synchronization, the clock loss flag will be set and cannot be cleared via the
CLRCKABF[y] bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLT0ICR register. The software operation sequence associated with the
clock loss detection function should be as follows:
 Enable the specified channel by setting CHEN=1
 Attempt to clear the clock absent flag (by setting CLRCKABF=1) until the clock absent flag is actually cleared
(CKABF=0). At this point, the transceiver is synchronized (signal clock is valid) and capable of receiving data
 Enable the clock absent function CKABEN=1 and the associated interrupt CKABIE=1 to detect whether the
SPI clock is lost
When using the SPI data format, clock loss detection is based on comparing the CKOUT signal generated from the
external input clock with the output clock. The external input clock signal in the input channel must change once
every 8 signal cycles of the CKOUT signal (controlled by the CKOUTDIV field in the R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1
register).

If a clock recovery error occurs during input, the clock absent flag is set to 1 (CKABF[y]=1) and an interrupt is
triggered (when CKABIE=1). After the clock absent flag is cleared (via CLRCKABF in the
R32_DFSDM_FLT0ICR register), the clock absent flag is reset.
External Serial Clock Frequency Measurement
By measuring the serial clock input frequency of the channel, the data rate from the external ΣΔ modulator can be
obtained in real time, which is critical for application purposes.
The external serial clock input frequency can be measured using a timer that counts the DFSDM clock (f )
DFSDMCLK
over one conversion duration. Counting begins at the first input data clock following conversion triggering (either
normal or injected) and ends at the last input data clock before conversion completion (when the conversion end
flag is set to 1). Upon conversion completion (JEOCF=1 or REOCF=1), the time per conversion (the interval
between the first and last serial samples) is updated in the CNVCNT[27:0] counter of register
R32_DFSDM_FLTxCNVTIMR. The user can then calculate the data rate based on the digital filter settings (FORD,
FOSR, IOSR, FAST). External serial frequency measurement ceases only when the filter is bypassed (FOSR=0,
only the integrator is active, and CNVCNT[27:0] in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCNVTIMR register equals 0).
For parallel data input (see Section 42.3.4: Parallel Data Input), the measured frequency represents the average input
data rate during a single conversion.

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
Note: When a conversion is interrupted (e.g., by disabling/enabling the selected channel), the interruption duration
is also counted in CNVCNT[27:0]. Therefore, to obtain accurate conversion timing results, it is recommended not
to interrupt conversions. It is recommended to measure the clock in continuous fast mode.

Channel Offset Settings
Each channel has its own offset setting (in the register), which will eventually be subtracted from each conversion
result (injection or normal) of a given channel. Offset correction is performed after the data is shifted to the right.
The offset value is stored as a 24-bit signed value in the OFFSET[23:0] field of R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR2 register.
Right Shift of Data
To align the result with a 24-bit value, each channel defines a series of right shifts that will be applied to each
conversion result (injection or normal) of a given channel. The right shift number is stored in bits DTRBS[4:0] of
R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR2 register.
Shift right rounds the result to the nearest integer value. The sign of the shifted result is preserved, so as to obtain
the result data in a valid 24-bit signed format.
42.3.3 Configuration Input Serial Interface
The following parameters must be configured for the input serial interface:
 Output clock prescaler. With the programmable prescaler, the output clock (range 2 to 256) can be generated
from the DFSDM clock. This setting is determined by the CKOUTDIV[7:0] bits in the
R32_DFSDM_CH0CFGR1 register.
 Type of serial interface and clock phase when input. Select SPI interface and sampling edge of input clock.
This option is specified by the SITP bit in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register.
 Input clock source selection. You can select an external source from the CKINy pin or an internal source from
the CKOUT pin. This selection is determined by the spikesel [1: 0] fields in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1
register.
 Final data right shift setting. Defines the right shift number of the final data to ensure that the result is aligned
V1.8 929

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
with the 24-bit value. This configuration is defined by the DTRBS[4:0] bits in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR2
register.
 Channel offset configuration. Set the analog offset (that is, the offset of the connected external σ δ modulator)
for a specific serial channel. This value is set by bits OFFSET[23:0] in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR2 register.
 Channel short detector and activation of clock missing function. In the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register,
the short-circuit detector of a given serial channel is enabled or disabled by the SCDEN bit, and the clock
missing detection is enabled or disabled by the CKABEN bit.
 Threshold configuration of analog watchdog filter and short circuit detector. Used to set the parameters of
channel analog watchdog filter and channel short circuit detector. These configurations are defined in the
R32_DFSDM_CHyAWSCDR register.
42.3.4 Parallel Data Input
Each input channel provides a register for 16-bit parallel data input (except serial data input). Each 16-bit parallel
input can only come from an internal data source:
 Internal ADC results (ADC1 and ADC2 only)
 Direct CPU/DMA write operation
Use the DATMPX[1:0] field of R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register to select whether to use serial or parallel data
input for a given channel. DATMPX[1:0] also defines parallel data source: internal ADC or write operation directly
by CPU/DMA.
Each channel contains a 32-bit data input register (R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR), in which 16 bits of data can be
written. The data is in a 16-bit signed format. These data can also be used as the input of a digital filter that accepts
16-bit parallel data.
If serial data input is selected (DATMPX[1:0]=0), the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register is write-protected.
Input from internal ADC (ADC1 and ADC2 only)
For parallel ADC data inputs (DATMPX[1:0]=1), the ADC[y+1] result is assigned to channel y input (ADC1
populates the R32_DFSDM_CH0DATINR register, ADC2 populates the R32_DFSDM_CH1DATINR register).
The conversion complete event from ADC[y+1] triggers an update to channel y's data (the parallel data from
ADC[y+1] is used as the next sample for the digital filter). When the conversion complete event occurs, the data
from ADC[y+1] is written to the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register (the INDAT0[15:0] field).
The data packing mode setting (DATPACK[1:0] in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register) has no effect on the
ADC data input.
Note: ADC Extension Specification: When the internal ADC is configured in interleaved mode (e.g., ADC1
interleaved with ADC2 - refer to ADC specification), each result from ADC1 or ADC2 is transmitted to the same
16-bit bus (i.e., ADC1's bus), which is connected to DFSDM Channel 0 (fixed connection). Therefore, DFSDM
channel 0 will carry double the input data rate (even samples from ADC1, odd samples from ADC2). Channel 1,
associated with ADC2, will remain idle.
Input from memory (written directly by CPU/DMA)
When CPU or DMA(DATMPX[1:0]=2) directly writes data into R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register, these data
can be used as input to process digital data streams from memory or peripherals.
Data can be written into R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register by CPU or DMA:
1) CPU data writing:
Input data is directly written into R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register by CPU.
2) DMA data writing:
V1.8 930

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
DMA should be configured as a memory-to-memory transfer mode to transfer the data in the buffer area of the
memory to the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register. The target memory address is the address of the
R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register. Data is transferred from memory to DFSDM parallel input at DMA transfer
speed.
This DMA is different from the DMA used to read the conversion result of DFSDM. These two DMA's can be used
at the same time. The first DMA (configured as memory-to-memory transfer) is used for input data writing, and the
second DMA (configured as peripheral-to-memory transfer) is used for data result reading.
The access to R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR can be 16-bit or 32-bit wide, allowing one or two samples to be loaded
in one write operation, respectively. The 32-bit input data register (R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR) can be filled with
one or two 16-bit data samples, depending on the data packing operation mode defined in the DATPACK[1:0] field
of R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register:
1) Standard Mode (DATPACK[1:0]=00b):
Only one sample is stored in the INDAT0[15:0] field of the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register, serving as input
data for channel y. The upper 16 bits (INDAT1[15:0]) are ignored and write-protected. The digital filter must
perform one input sample (via INDAT0[15:0]) to clear the data register after CPU/DMA fill. This mode combines
with 16-bit CPU/DMA access to the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register to load one sample per write operation.
2) Interleaved Mode (DATPACK[1:0]=01b):
The R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register functions as two sample buffers. The first sample is stored in
INDAT0[15:0], and the second sample is stored in INDAT1[15:0]. The digital filter must perform two input samples
through channel y to clear the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register. This mode is combined with 32-bit CPU/DMA
access to the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register to load two samples per write operation.
3) Dual-Channel Mode (DATPACK[1:0]=10b):
Write 2 samples into the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register. Data in INDAT0[15:0] is used for channel y, while
data in INDAT1[15:0] is used for channel y+1. Data in INDAT1[15:0] is automatically copied to INDAT0[15:0] of
the next (y+1) channel data register (DFSDM_CH[y+1]DATINR). The digital filter must perform two samples (one
from channel y and one from channel (y+1)) to clear the R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register.
Dual-channel mode configuration (DATPACK[1:0]=10b) is only possible for even channel numbers (y=0). If an
odd channel (y=1) is set to dual-channel mode, both the INDAT0[15:0] and INDAT1[15:0] sections for that channel
are write-protected. If an even channel is set to dual-channel mode, the next odd channel must be set to standard
mode (DATPACK[1:0]=00b) to properly interface with the even channel.
Please refer to the figure below for the data mode of R32_DFSDM_CHyDATINR register and the allocation of
channel data samples.

42.3.5 Channel Selection
There are 2 multiplex channels, which can be selected for injection channel group conversion and/or conventional
channel conversion.
The injection channel group can select any or all of the 2 channels. JCHG[1:0] in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxJCHGR
register selects the injection group channel, where JCHG[y]=1 indicates that channel y has been selected.
Injection conversion can work in scan mode (JSCAN=1) or single mode (JSCAN=0). In scan mode, each selected
channel will be converted in turn. The lowest channel (channel 0, if selected) is converted first, and then the next
higher channel is converted until all channels selected by JCHG[1:0] are converted. In single mode (JSCAN=0),
only one selected channel will be converted, and the channel selection will be moved to the next channel. When
JSCAN=0, writing to JCHG[1:0] will reset the channel selection to the lowest channel selected.
Injection conversion can be initiated by software or triggers. Such conversions are never interrupted by regular
conversions.
Conventional channels only select one of the two channels. The RCH bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register
indicates the selected channel.
General conversions can only be initiated by software (not by triggers). When an injection conversion is requested,
the continuous regular conversion sequence is temporarily interrupted.
Attempting a conversion on a disabled channel (CHEN=0 in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register) will cause the
conversion to never complete, as no input data is provided (no clock signal). In this case, either enable the given
channel (CHEN=1 in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register) or stop the conversion (by setting DFEN=0 in the
R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register).
42.3.6 Digital Filter Configuration
DFSDM includes a Sincx-type digital filter implementation. This Sincx filter performs filtering on the input digital
data stream, resulting in a reduced output data rate (decimation) and increased output data resolution. The Sincx
digital filter can be configured to achieve the desired output data rate and desired output data resolution.
Configurable parameters include:
 Filter order/type: (Refer to FORD[2:0] bits in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxFCR register):
- FastSinc
- Sinc1
- Sinc2
- Sinc3
- Sinc4
- Sinc5
 Filter oversampling/decimation rate: (Refer to FOSR[9:0] bits in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxFCR register):
- FOSR=1-1024——Applicable to FastSinc filters and Sincx filters where x=FORD=1..3
- FOSR=1-215——Applicable to Sincx filters where x=FORD=4
- FOSR=1-73——Applicable to Sincx filters where x=FORD=5

42.3.7 Integrator Unit
The integrator will further improve the decimation rate and resolution of the data from the digital filter. For a given
number of data samples from the filter, the integrator simply sums them.
The over-sampling rate parameter of the integrator defines how many data are summed as a data output of the
integrator.  IOSR  can  be  set  in  the  range  of  1~256  (refer  to  the  description  of  IOSR[3:0]  bits  in
R32_DFSDM_FLTxFCR register).

42.3.8 Analog Watchdog
The analog watchdog is used to trigger an external signal (open circuit or interrupt) when it reaches or exceeds a
given upper threshold or reaches or falls below a given lower threshold. Interrupt/event/open circuit generation can
then be invoked.
Each analog watchdog monitors the serial data receiver output (after the watchdog filter is simulated on each channel)
or the data output register (current injection or general conversion result) according to the AWFSEL bit setting (in
the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register). Whether the input channels need to be monitored by analog watchdog X can
be selected by AWDCH[1:0] in R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR2 register.
Analog watchdog conversions on input channels are independent of standard conversions. In standard conversion
mode, the analog watchdog employs its own filter and signal processing on each input channel, unaffected by
injection or regular master conversions. In continuous conversion mode, analog watchdog conversions are
performed on selected input channels to maintain channel monitoring even when injection or regular master
conversions are paused (RCIP=0, JCIP=0).
The upper threshold and lower threshold registers are compared against a given data value (set via the AWHT[23:0]
bits of the R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWHTR register and the AWLT[23:0] bits of the R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWLTR
register).
You can choose two situations to compare the threshold register with the data value:
 Option 1: In this case, the input data is taken from the final output data register (AWFSEL=0). This choice has
the following characteristics:
- High input data resolution (up to 24 bits)
- Slow response time—not suitable for fast-response applications such as overcurrent detection
- For comparison purposes, final data requires shift and offset correction
- Final data becomes available only after executing a normal or injected main conversion
- Operates with parallel input data sources (DATMPX[1:0] ≠ 0 in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1
register)
 Option 2: In this case, the input data is taken from the output of any serial data receiver (AWFSEL=1). This
choice has the following characteristics:
- Serial data input is processed through a dedicated analog watchdog Sincx channel filter. The filter's
oversampling rate (1..32) and filter order (1..3) are configurable (refer to the AWFOSR[4:0] and
AWFORD[1:0] bits in the R32_DFSDM_CHyAWSCDR register).
- Lower resolution (up to 16 bits)
- Fast response time—suitable for applications requiring rapid response, such as overcurrent/overvoltage
detection
- Data is provided in continuous mode, independent of regular or injected main conversion activity
During input channel monitoring (AWFSEL=1), data for threshold comparison is sourced from the channel selected
via the AWDCH[1:0] field (R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR2 register). The filter result from each selected channel is
compared against a threshold pair (AWHT[23:0]/AWLT[23:0]). At this point, only the upper 16 bits
(AWHT[23:8]/AWLT[23:8]) define the 16-bit threshold compared against the analog watchdog filter output, as the
data from the analog watchdog filter has a maximum resolution of 16 bits. In this case (AWFSEL=1), the
AWHT[7:0]/AWLT[7:0] bits are not compared.
The parameters for the analog watchdog filter configuration of each input channel (filter order AWFORD[1:0] and
filter oversampling rate AWFOSR[4:0]) are set in the R32_DFSDM_CHyAWSCDR register.
The analog watchdog filter data for channel y can be read via firmware from the WDATA[15:0] field of the
V1.8 934

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
DFSDM_CHyWDATR register. If CHEN=1 in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register, this analog watchdog filter
data is continuously converted at a data rate determined by the analog watchdog filter settings and the channel input
clock frequency.
The analog watchdog filter operates similarly to a conventional fast continuous conversion (without integrator). The
number of serial samples required for the analog watchdog filter to output a result (with channel input clock
frequency fCKIN) is:
First conversion:
For Sincx filters (x=1..5): Number of samples = [F *(F +1)+2]
OSR ORD
For FastSinc filters: Number of samples = [F *4+2+1]
OSR
Subsequent conversion:
For Sincx and FastSinc filters: Number of samples = [FOSR*FORD]
Among them:
F , or Filter Oversampling Ratio: F = AWFOSR[4:0] + 1 (refer to the R32_DFSDM_CHyAWSCDR register)
OSR OSR
F , or Filter Order: F = AWFORD[1:0] (refer to the R32_DFSDM_CHyAWSCDR register)
ORD ORD
For output data register monitoring (AWFSEL=0), comparison occurs after completing the final data right shift and
offset correction (refer to the OFFSET[23:0] and DTRBS[4:0] fields in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR2 register).
The comparison occurs after each injection or regular conversion of the channel selected by the AWDCH[1:0] field
(in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR2 register).
The status of simulated watchdog events is reflected in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWSR register, which locks the
given event. The AWHTF[y]=1 flag indicates whether the AWHT[23:0] value has been exceeded on channel y. The
AWLFTF[y]=1 flag indicates whether the AWLT[23:0] value has been exceeded on channel y. Events latched in the
R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWSR register are cleared by writing a 1 to the corresponding clear bit CLRAWHTF[y] or
CLRAWLTF[y] in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxAWCFR register.
42.3.9 Short Circuit Detector
The purpose of the short-circuit detector is to signal within an extremely fast response time when an analog signal
reaches saturation (exceeds full-scale range) and remains there for a specified duration. This feature detects short-
circuit or open-circuit faults (e.g., overcurrent or overvoltage). Interrupts/events/open-circuit generation can be
invoked.
The short-circuit detector's input data is derived from the channel transceiver output.
Each input channel features an incrementing counter that tallies consecutive 0s or 1s on the serial data receiver
output. If the received data stream changes (data signal conversions from 1 to 0 or from 0 to 1), the counter is reset.
A short-circuit event is triggered when the counter reaches the short-circuit threshold register value (SCDT[7:0] bits
in the R32_DFSDM_CHyAWSCDR register). Each input channel is equipped with a dedicated short-circuit detector.
Continuous monitoring for any channel can be enabled by setting the SCDEN bit (in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1
register). Each channel has its own short-circuit detector configuration (threshold bits SCDT[7:0], status bits
SCDF[1:0], status clear bits CLRSCDF[1:0]). When the corresponding channel y is disabled (CHEN[y]=0), the
status flag SCDF[y] can also be cleared by hardware.
For each channel, short-circuit detector events can be assigned to the break output signals DFSDM_BK[1:0]. Two
break outputs can be assigned to a single short-circuit detector event. The break signals are assigned to a given
channel's short-circuit detector event via the BKSCD[1:0] field in the R32_DFSDM_CHyAWSCDR register.
If parallel input data channels are selected (DATMPX[1:0] ≠ 0 in the R32_DFSDM_CHyCFGR1 register), the
short-circuit detector cannot be used.
A total of two break outputs are available (shared with the analog watchdog function).

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
42.3.10 Extreme Value Detector
The Extreme Value Detector captures the minimum and maximum values (peak-to-peak values) of the final output
data word.
If the output data word exceeds the value stored in the maximum value register of the extremum detector
(EXMAX[23:0] bits in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMAX register), this register is updated with the current output
data word value, and the channel storing its data is indicated in the EXMAXCH bit (of the
R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMAX register).
If the output data word is less than the value stored in the extremum detector minimum register (EXMIN[23:0] bits
in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMIN register), this register is updated with the current output data word value, and
the channel storing its data is indicated by the EXMINCH bit (in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMIN register).
The minimum and maximum value register values can be refreshed by software (by reading the
R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMAX or R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMIN registers). After refresh, the minimum value data
register (R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMIN) is filled with 0x7FFFFF (maximum positive value), and the maximum value
register (R32_DFSDM_FLTxEXMAX) is filled with 0x800000 (minimum negative value).
The extremum detector performs comparison operations only after completing right shift and offset data correction.
For each extremum detector, the input channels involved in extremum calculation are selected by the EXCH[1:0]
bits (in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR2 register).

42.3.12 Signed Data Format
Each channel of the DFSDM input serial channel can be connected to an external ΣΔ modulator. An external ΣΔ
modulator is configured with two differential inputs (positive and negative), which can be used for either differential
measurements or single-ended signal measurements.
It is always assumed that the ΣΔ modulator's output uses a signed format (i.e., the 0/1 data stream from the ΣΔ
modulator represents the values -1 and +1).
Signed Data Format in Registers: Data stored in the final output data register, analog watchdog register, extreme
value detector register, and offset correction register are all in signed format. The most significant bit (MSB) of the
output data word indicates the sign of the value (using two's complement format).
42.3.13 Start Conversion
The method to start the injection conversion is as follows:
 Software: write 1 to JSWSTART in R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register.
 Trigger: with JEXTEN activated, select the trigger signal through JEXTSEL[3:0] and determine the effective
edge (refer to R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register).
 If JSYNC is set to 1, DFSDM_FLT0 will start injection conversion synchronously: for DFSDM_FLTx(x>0),
injection conversion will start automatically in DFSDM_FLT0; The injection conversion is triggered by
software (set to 1 by the JSWSTART bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLT0CR2 register). Each injection conversion
in DFSDM_FLTx(x>0) will be performed according to its local settings (such as JSCAN and JCHG).
 Only one injection conversion is allowed at a specific time. Therefore, if an injection conversion request has
been issued but not yet completed, any subsequent startup request will be ignored.
The way to start a regular conversion is as follows:
 Software: write 1 to RSWSTART in R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register.
 If RSYNC=1, use DFSDM_FLT0 to start synchronously: for DFSDM_FLTx(x>0), normal conversion will
start automatically in DFSDM_FLT0; The normal conversion is triggered by software (set to 1 by the
RSWSTARTT bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLT0CR2 register). Every regular conversion in DFSDM_FLTx(x>0)
will be performed according to its local configuration settings (RCONT, RCH, etc.).
42.3.14 Continuous and Fast Continuous Mode
If RCONT in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register is set to 1, normal conversion will be performed in continuous
mode. RCONT=1 means that after writing 1 to RSWSTART, the channel selected by the RCH bit is repeatedly
V1.8 937

CH32H417 Reference Manual https://wch-ic.com
converted.
Normal conversion performed in continuous mode can be stopped by writing 0 to RCONT. After the RCONT is
cleared, the ongoing conversion will be stopped immediately.
In continuous mode, the data rate can be increased by setting bit 1 of the FAST position in the
R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register. At this time, if a continuous conversion is performed on a channel, the filter does
not need to be refilled with new refresh data because the internal filter data is valid. This data was previously
obtained by sampling continuous data. The speed increase is related to the selected filter order. After initiating
continuous conversion with RSWSTART=1, the initial conversion in Fast mode (FAST=1) is performed fully
(identical to FAST=0), followed by subsequent conversions completed at shorter intervals.
Conversion time in continuous mode:
When FAST=0 (or fast conversion when FAST=1):
For Sincx filter:
t=CNVCNT/f =[F *（2IOSR+F +1）+2]/f
DFSDMCLK OSR ORD CKIN
For FastSinc filter:
t=CNVCNT/f =[F *（2IOSR+5）+2]/f
DFSDMCLK OSR CKIN
When FAST=1 (except for the first conversion):
For Sincx and FastSinc filter:
t=CNVCNT/f =[F *2IOSR]/f
DFSDMCLK OSR CKIN
When FOSR=FOSR[9:0]+1=1 (filter bypass, only integrator is effective):

CKIN
Continuous mode is not applicable to injection conversion. Injection conversion can be initiated via timer triggering
to simulate continuous mode with precise timing.
If a regular continuous conversion is in progress (RCONT=1), and if a write access is made to the
R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register requesting a regular continuous conversion (RCONT=1), the regular continuous
conversion will restart from the next conversion cycle (similar to a new regular continuous conversion being applied
to a new channel selection, even if no change is made to the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register).
42.3.15 Request Priority
Injected conversions take precedence over regular conversions. An ongoing regular conversion is immediately
interrupted by an injected conversion request; this regular conversion will resume after the injected conversion
completes.
If an injected conversion is pending or in progress, no other injected conversion can be initiated: requests to start an
injected conversion (via JSWSTART or trigger) are ignored as long as bit JCIP (in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxISR
register) is set to 1.
Similarly, if a regular conversion is pending or in progress, no other regular conversion can be initiated: requests to
start a regular conversion (using RSWSTART) are ignored as long as bit RCIP (in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxISR
register) is set to 1.
However, if an injection conversion is requested during a regular conversion, the regular conversion stops
immediately and the injection conversion begins. The regular conversion restarts afterward, and this delayed restart
is indicated by the RPEND bit.
Injection conversion takes precedence over regular conversion because it can temporarily interrupt a continuous
sequence of regular conversions. Upon completing the injection conversion sequence, if RCONT remains set to 1,
the continuous regular conversion will restart (the RPEND bit will issue a delayed start signal based on the result
V1.8 938

CH32H417 Reference Manual                                          https://wch-ic.com
of the first regular conversion).
Priority is also critical when initiating related operations through identical write operations to DFSDM, or if multiple
operations remain pending at the conclusion of other operations. For example, assuming an injection conversion is
in progress (JCIP=1), a single write operation to R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 writes 1 to RSWSTART to request a
regular conversion. Upon completion of the injection sequence, the priority indicates execution of the subsequent
regular conversion, with the corresponding delayed start indicated via the RPEND bit.

42.3.16 Power Consumption Optimization in Running Mode
To reduce power consumption, the DFSDM filter and integrator automatically enter idle state (RCIP=0, JCIP=0)
when not used for conversion.

42.5 DFSDM DMA Transfer
To reduce CPU intervention, DMA transfers can be used to transfer conversions to memory. DMA transfers for
injected conversions are enabled by setting the JDMAEN bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register. DMA
transfers for regular conversions are enabled by setting the RDMAEN bit in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxCR1 register.
Note: With DMA transfers, interrupt flags (JEOCF or REOCF bits in the R32_DFSDM_FLTxISR register) are
automatically  cleared  at  the  end  of  an  injection  or  regular  conversion  because  DMA  is  reading  the
R32_DFSDM_FLTxJDATAR or R32_DFSDM_FLTxRDATAR registers.

Injection channel group selection:
00: Neither Channel 0 nor Channel 1 belongs to the
injection group;

10: Channel 1 belongs to the injection group;

|                   |     |     |     | If  JSCAN=1,   | each  | selected  | channel  | is  converted  |         |      |
| ----------------- | --- | --- | --- | -------------- | ----- | --------- | -------- | -------------- | ------- | ---- |

| [1:0]  JCHG[1:0]  |     |     | RW  |                |       |           |          |                |         | 01b  |
selected) is converted first, and the largest selected
channel is converted last.
If JSCAN=0, only one selected channel is converted,
then the channel selection moves to the next channel.
If JSCAN=0, writing to JCHG resets the channel
selection to the smallest selected channel.
At least one channel must always be selected for the
injection group. If a write operation sets all JCHG bits
to zero, the write operation is ignored.

Chapter 43 LCD-TFT Display Controller (LTDC)
LCD-TFT (Thin Film Transistor-Liquid Crystal Display) Display Controller (LTDC) mainly provides parallel
digital RGB, horizontal synchronization, vertical synchronization, pixel clock and data enable signals, which can
be used as output signals to interface with different LCD and TFT panels.
43.1 Main Features
 Provide 2 display layers, each containing a proprietary 8×256-bit FIFO
 Support color lookup tables (CLUT) with up to 256 colors per layer
 Support programmable timing for different display panels
 Support programmable background color
 Support programmable polarity for HSYNC, VSYNC, and data enable signals
 Each display layer supports up to 8 input colors
 Flexible blending between 2 layers using alpha values (per-pixel or constant)
 Support chroma key (transparent color)
 Support programmable window position and size
 Support thin-film transistor (TFT) color displays
 Support up to 3 programmable interrupt timers

43.3 Function Description
43.3.1 LTDC Synchronization Timing
The LTDC interface is a synchronous data interface comprising pixel clock, pixel data, and horizontal and vertical

sync signals. Figure 43-2 illustrates the configurable timing parameters generated by the LTDC synchronous timing
generator module.

Note: (1) HSYNC and VSYNC denote horizontal and vertical sync widths, respectively; HBP and HFP denote
horizontal back-edge period and horizontal front-edge period, respectively; VBP and VFP denote vertical back-
edge period and vertical front-edge period, respectively.
(2) When LTDC is enabled, the generated timing uses the X/Y=0/0 position as the first horizontal sync pixel within
the vertical sync region, followed by the back edge, active data display region, and front edge.
(3) When LTDC is disabled, the timing generator module resets to X=total width-1 and Y=total height-1, holding
the previous pixel during the vertical sync phase and before FIFO refresh. Consequently, only blanking data is
continuously output.
An example of synchronization timing configuration is as follows:
1) LCD-TFT timing (to be extracted from the panel datasheet);
2) Horizontal and vertical sync width: 0xA pixels, 0x2-1 lines;
3) Horizontal and vertical trailing edge: 0x14 pixels, 0x2 lines;
4) Effective width and effective height: 0x140 pixels, 0xF0 lines (320x240);
5) Horizontal leading edge: 0xA pixels;
6) Vertical leading edge: 0x4 lines;
The value programmed in the LTDC timing register will be:
1) R32_LTDC_SSCR register: Programmed to 0x00090001. (HSW[11:0] is 0xA-1 and VSH[10:0] is 0x2-1);
2) R32_LTDC_BPCR register: Programmed to 0x001D0003. (AHBP[11:0] is 0x1D (0xA + 0x14-1), AVBP[10:0]
is 0x3 (0x2 + 0x2-1));
